93717dc36dea77eb: IN conjunction with the 35th Malaysian Film Festival to be held this Saturday, the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) recently spotlighted veteran performers A.R. Badul and Norlia Ghani with a screening of 'Tuan Badul' (1979) and a forum celebrating their contributions to Malaysian cinema.
The screening offered a chance to revisit a piece of local film history, while the forum drew attention to the realities facing the people who helped shape it.
But beyond nostalgia, their comments at the event raised a more pressing question: how can the industry keep making room for veteran artistes who still have the desire and ability to work?
For Badul, the answer lies in creating more meaningful opportunities for veteran actors. For Norlia, it is equally important that their contributions be recognised before they fade into memory.
Their perspectives may differ, but both point to the same issue: veteran artistes should not have to rely solely on nostalgia to remain part of the entertainment industry.
A tribute can bring the past into focus, but its real value lies in what happens afterwards.
If the industry is serious about honouring its veterans, it must do more than celebrate their achievements. It must continue to give them reasons and opportunities to step in front of the camera.
The event also served as a reminder that recognition should not be reserved for the end of an artiste's career, or worse, come only after their passing.
For both veteran actors, the tribute was meaningful because it acknowledged that they still have something to contribute.
A CHANCE TO KEEP WORKING
Badul, whose real name is Armaya Aman Ramlie, said the most meaningful form of appreciation is not applause or public recognition, but the opportunity to continue doing what he loves.
"We greatly appreciate the support of the public, but what means more to artistes is the opportunity to continue working and contributing their talents for as long as they are needed."
It is a sentiment that underscored his proposal for a dedicated fund to support drama series featuring veteran performers.
While telefilms have provided some opportunities, Badul, 77, believes the format can be restrictive, with limited roles and screen time for older actors.
A longer-running series, on the other hand, could accommodate a larger ensemble, allowing more veterans to take part and giving their characters room to develop.

"If we create a drama series with more episodes, there will be greater opportunities. Dozens of veteran artistes could be given roles according to the storyline. They would not always have to play mothers or fathers and appear in only a few scenes," he added.

His suggestion is rooted in a belief that experience should not be mistaken for diminished ability. Veteran performers, he pointed out, still possess the resilience, energy and passion to work in front of the camera. What they need is a production environment willing to make space for them.

The proposal received an encouraging response from Finas chairman Datuk Hans Isaac, who said the agency was prepared to consider adapting its Veteran Artistes Supertelefilm Fund (STAR) to support the production of drama series.
Hans said he would bring the matter to the Finas committee and the Communications Ministry for discussion. He also suggested that a 30-episode series could involve 10 to 15 veteran actors.
According to Hans, the STAR initiative had already supported 10 telefilm projects for broadcast on Radio Televisyen Malaysia. Expanding the format could be a way of building on that effort.
BEFORE THEY ARE FORGOTTEN
For Norlia, the recent tribute carried a more personal significance.

The actress — fondly remembered by generations of viewers for playing Joyah in the long-running and popular television drama 'Opah' — admitted that being away from television and film for an extended period had made her wonder whether audiences still remembered her.
She was touched by the recognition from Finas.

"Usually, when you have not appeared on television or in films for a long time, people forget you. So, when I received this recognition, I felt that people still remembered Norlia Ghani and appreciated my acting," she said
Her words reflect the concern shared by many performers, who built decades-long careers only to find that opportunities become less frequent as they grow older.
The problem is not necessarily a lack of interest or ability, but the industry's tendency to move on to younger faces.
Norlia was particularly candid about how recognition is often delayed until after an artiste has died.
"Only after they have died do people want to give them titles such as ʻTan Sri' or ʻDatuk'. By then, it is too late," she said.
Celebrating veteran performers while they are still around is a simple but important way of acknowledging their place in the industry's history.
A NEW STAGE ON TIKTOK
Norlia is not waiting for television producers to offer her the next opportunity.
Approaching her 78th birthday next month, she has found another way to stay connected with audiences through TikTok.

The platform has become a space where she can interact with fans, produce content and earn an income through product reviews, food promotions and other collaborations. She has also received invitations to events, while some of her videos have attracted millions of views.

Norlia said the move was partly prompted by the need to manage her health. Although she continues to receive acting offers, she has become more selective because filming can involve long hours and demanding schedules.
"I need to take care of my health as I am no longer as strong as I used to be. Occasionally, I will accept acting offers. If there are none, I'll focus on TikTok."
Norlia has discovered that creating digital content can be financially worthwhile.
She acknowledged that her TikTok income now exceeds what she earns from acting, partly because product review assignments can be completed in a shorter time.
"Sometimes, it takes one or two days to finish the work and get payment. With episodic dramas, it takes longer."
For Norlia, there is little distinction between the two forms of work. Both require her to face a camera, communicate with an audience and draw on the performance skills she has developed.
She is also unfazed by views that older people should not be too active on social media. To her, nothing is embarrassing about finding an honest way to earn a living.
Her willingness to embrace a new platform is a reminder that staying relevant does not always mean returning to the same stage. Sometimes, it means finding a different one.

ffff5dd5794fc656: KUALA LUMPUR: The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) has chosen Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd to take over Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) at an estimated price of RM4.3 billion, sources told Berita Harian.
Achi Jaya is understood to have beaten SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd for the takeover, two companies with larger-scale plantation operations.
According to the sources, the decision has been made although details of the acquisition structure, equity interest involved and payment terms have yet to be made public.
The amount also drew attention when compared with Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd's (KLK) proposed acquisition of BPlant in 2023, which valued the plantation company's entire equity at about RM3.47 billion.
On Aug 24, 2023, KLK entered into an agreement to buy a 33 per cent stake in BPlant from Boustead Holdings Bhd at RM1.55 per share, in a transaction valued at RM1.15 billion.
However, the transaction was terminated on Oct 4 that year.
According to its 2025 Integrated Report, SD Guthrie has a total land bank of 703,115 hectares across several countries.
Of this, 557,258 hectares comprise oil palm planted areas, including 292,122 hectares in Malaysia.
Tradewinds Plantation, meanwhile, has a total land bank of 156,138 hectares, witj about 87 per cent being planted with oil palm and rubber.
In comparison, the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification documents for Achi Jaya recorded 11,702 hectares of oil palm planted area within the scope of its audit in November 2025.
However, this figure does not necessarily cover the company's entire operations.
BPlant, meanwhile, reportedly has a land bank of 97,500 hectare, including about 72,200 hectares of oil palm planted area.
Based on the planted area recorded in Achi Jaya's MSPO audit, the company could potentially manage 83,902 hectares of oil palm planted area following its acquisition.
This estimate, however, is based on the assumption that all of BPlant's oil palm planted areas are included in the transaction and that there is no overlap in assets.

If the RM4.3 billion refers to BPlant's entire equity value, the figure would be about RM830 million or 23.9 per cent higher than the RM3.47 billion valuation under KLK's proposed transaction in 2023.

However, a direct comparison can only be made once Achi Jaya's transaction structure is confirmed, including whether the RM4.3 billion price tag covers BPlant's entire equity or only a specific stake.
Achi Jaya Plantations is a privately held company incorporated on Feb 10, 2001, and is involved in oil palm cultivation and milling, as well as hotel management and operations.
According to its November 2025 MSPO audit report, Achi Jaya's operations within the scope of certification comprise Sungei Gerchang Estate, Johore Labis Estate and Claire Estate in Chaah, Johor.

LTAT recently come under the spotlight in Parliament after Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin confirmed the sale of its leasehold interest in a piece of land in Ampang Hilir, Kuala Lumpur, to the US government for RM420 million.
Mohamed Khaled was reported to have said on Oct 26 that the transaction, which was conducted through a tender process, was for the construction of a new US embassy.
He explained that the disposal was part of LTAT's efforts to rebalance its asset portfolio, while ensuring compliance with relevant policies, procedures and governance requirements.
The ownership of the land remains with the Federal Lands Commissioner, as the transaction involved only the leasehold interest.

Under the proposed BPlant acquisition, the transaction value, payment terms and the buyer's ability to manage the plantation assets are among the key considerations in safeguarding the long-term interests of LTAT, members of the Malaysian armed forces and its contributors.

31782bdd7ab27403: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Platform providers removed 13,883 deepfake items between January 1, 2024, and October 31 this year following takedown requests by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) based on public complaints, Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil told Parliament today.
Of these, 1,178 items involved political leaders, Fahmi said when outlining regulatory and enforcement measures against artificial intelligence (AI) misuse.
He said that under the Risk Mitigation Code, which took effect on June 1 this year, licensed service providers are required to establish mechanisms to identify, assess and address harmful content.
The code also requires AI-generated or manipulated images, audio and video likely to be mistaken for authentic content to be clearly labelled, and that users be given accessible reporting tools.

“On the prevention front, the government, through the MCMC, is also implementing the Safe Internet campaign to raise public awareness and digital literacy, particularly in identifying deepfake content, identity impersonation, and AI-generated false information,” he said during Question Time.
“The campaign also emphasises the importance of verifying information before believing or sharing it, to prevent the public from falling victim to online scams and information manipulation.”

On enforcement, Fahmi said the MCMC investigated 61 cases involving AI misuse under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) between January 1, 2025, and October 31 this year.
Of these, 10 cases were brought to court, while compounds totalling RM755,000 were issued in seven cases and 17 warning letters were served.
Six of the 10 court cases have been decided, with fines totalling RM19,500.
He did not say what action was taken on the remaining 27 cases.

398e90b0c262ea2d: TOKYO: Japan said Tuesday it scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace, and lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow.
The aircraft entered Japan's airspace close to Okinoshima, in the southwestern area of Fukuoka, shortly after 4am Tuesday.
Japan's self defence force scrambled fighter jets to warn the "suspected Russian" planes, top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.

"The violation of our national airspace by Russian aircraft is not only a grave infringement of our country's sovereignty, but also a threat to our security and is completely unacceptable," Kihara said.
"We lodged a very stern protest with Russia through diplomatic channels and strongly demanded measures to prevent any recurrence," Kihara added.
Relations with Moscow have soured in recent weeks following the arrest of a Japanese journalist on spying allegations and the seizure of Japan Tobacco's Russian assets.
Kihara said the aircraft travelled through the Tsushima Strait and went between Yonaguni island and Taiwan before heading to the Pacific.
Tokyo's announcement comes after South Korea said it deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical manoeuvres after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone.

The Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) in Seoul said an unspecified number of Russian aircraft entered and later exited the Korea Air Defence Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, in the early hours of Tuesday.
An air defence identification zone is not sovereign airspace but a buffer area in which countries identify approaching aircraft for security purposes.
Military aircraft are generally expected to notify the relevant country before entering its air defence zone, although such notification is not legally required.
Seoul said the Russian aircraft did not violate South Korean airspace.
Japan lodged a "very serious protest" with Moscow in 2024 after a Russian patrol plane entered its airspace three times. That was the first confirmed incursion since 2019.

Russia and Japan have a decades-old dispute over the status of a string of islands in the Pacific Ocean, but their relations has deteriorated further since Tokyo joined global sanctions against Moscow over the Ukraine war.

In August, Japan protested Russian president Vladimir Putin's visit to the far-eastern Kuril islands - a disputed territory known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.
It was the first visit to the islands by a Russian president since Dmitry Medvedev in 2010.
Tokyo also protested in August against Russia's announcement that Moscow would conduct missile tests off one of the disputed islands visited by Putin.
0e8578ece5a960c2: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — French President Emmanuel Macron, on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning.
Macron, accompanied by his wife Brigitte Macron, arrived at 9.30 am and was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Also present were both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
The ceremony began with the French and Malaysian national anthems, performed by the Central Band of the Royal Malay Regiment (RAMD) under the baton of Captain Muhamad Fauzee Japar.
Macron then inspected a guard of honour comprising three officers and 103 other ranks from the First Battalion of RAMD, commanded by Major Adibadiuezshah Ahmad.

Notably, the welcome was held at the historic Dataran Merdeka, a site synonymous with the nation’s struggle for independence and one of the capital’s defining landmarks, rather than in Putrajaya or at Istana Negara, where previous official ceremonies for foreign leaders have been staged.
This is Macron’s first official trip to Malaysia since he assumed the French presidency in May 2017.
It is expected to open a new chapter in Malaysia-France relations, with both countries seeking to elevate their existing ties to a Strategic Partnership.
Priority areas of cooperation include defence and security, critical minerals, energy transition, aeronautics and aerospace, AI, cybersecurity and semiconductors.
The visit builds on the momentum from Anwar’s official trip to France in July 2025, the first by a Malaysian head of government to the country in 15 years.

France is Malaysia’s 10th-largest trading partner and its third-largest within the European Union, with bilateral trade reaching €4.7 billion (approximately RM21.23 billion) in 2025, up 11 per cent from 2024. — Bernama

1b705e0cfd681f66: WASHINGTON: Speculation over Anthropic's stock market valuation has highlighted one of the riskiest bets in finance: trying to put a price on the future of artificial intelligence.
A few days before its initial public offering, the maker of the AI agent Claude said it was aiming for a market capitalization of up to US$1.4 trillion.
That figure would put the young company among the largest stock market debuts on record, though it falls short of the US$2 trillion some estimates had floated until a few weeks ago.

Since then, concern about AI development and profits has swept the market. OpenAI, a rival which plans to go public in 2027, is valued at US$1.025 trillion on the private market, according to US media reports.
There are two main ways to value a company, said Michelle Lowry, a finance professor at Drexel University. The first is to estimate how much cash the company will bring in over the coming years.
Money expected far in the future counts for less than money today, especially when it is uncertain, so those future amounts are reduced to work out what the company is worth now.
The second compares the company with similar listed firms. If those firms are valued at, say, five times their annual revenue, the same ratio is applied to the company being valued.
Both methods are well established, but "in the case of Anthropic, both of these approaches are quite difficult," Lowry told AFP.
Like most AI companies, Anthropic is still burning through cash and has not found a path to profitability, which makes its future cash flows hard to forecast.
It also has few listed peers. The closest is SpaceX, which made a record debut on Wall Street in June with a valuation of US$1.77 trillion.
But that comparison is imperfect, since the Elon Musk-led company combines a social network, space operations and an AI lab. SpaceX also rides on Musk's star power among retail investors.
'Back and forth'

So how was the US$1.4 trillion figure set? "There's some back and forth process" between companies seeking to go public and institutional investors, said Minmo Gahng, an assistant professor of finance at Cornell University.
Investment banks act as intermediaries between the two sides, he said, in a process that can be very time-consuming.
A company's valuation is its share price multiplied by the number of shares outstanding. A company going public wants that price as high as possible, since it determines how much money it raises.
But it also has to leave enough room to attract buyers, since weak demand would drag down the stock.
Investors, for their part, want to be sure they can later sell their stakes at a profit -- and are hoping for a "pop," or sharp rise in the share price, on the first day of trading.
Speaking Friday with JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon, Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei cited a company motto when discussing the IPO: "underpromise and overdeliver."
He also said the company was going public mainly because it needs funding. Anthropic is set to raise a total of US$90 billion through the offering, money it plans to use to develop cutting-edge AI.
'No guarantee'

Jay Ritter, an IPO specialist at the University of Florida, said investors accept such valuations because a handful of companies, such as Amazon, Alphabet and Nvidia, have shown "you can earn profits of US$100 billion a year or more without competition eroding those profits."
But there is "no guarantee" that Anthropic will do the same, he warned.
"It could be the case that 10 years from now, Anthropic will have been left in the dust where nobody is using frontier large language models because open source models are good enough and cheap."

Anthropic's growth has already shown signs of slowing and 90 pages of its IPO prospectus are devoted to risks facing the future of the company -- and even of humanity -- depending on the direction AI takes.

7b14fa07e777fd79: SAN JOSE: Costa Rican independent journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who had called out alleged ties between drug traffickers and politicians on social media, was shot dead on Monday outside the capital San Jose, authorities said.
Two men riding on a motorcycle opened fire on Rodriguez as he was driving through the town of Santo Domingo de Heredia, police chief Raul Rivera said.
Rodriguez, 50, had reported receiving several death threats from drug trafficking groups.

He would name drug lords by their full names and claimed to have provided reports to the US Drug Enforcement Administration regarding links between drug traffickers and powerful figures in politics and business.

When President Laura Fernandez was running for office last year, she sued Rodriguez for defamation after he posted a video claiming her home had been built with money allegedly provided by a drug trafficker.
"Regardless of the content of his statements, what happened today in our country is a stain on freedom of expression," Fernandez said in a video released by her office.
Rodriguez ran for president in 2022 but his nomination was rejected by electoral authorities on technical grounds.
He also accused his ex-wife of being involved in drug trafficking. She has filed a complaint alleging he sexually abused their children.
The Costa Rican Journalists' Association condemned his killing and demanded "a swift investigation".

"All evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica – a person who published information about organised crime in the country," the association's president, Yanancy Noguera, told AFP.
In recent years, Costa Rica has gone from being a drug transit point to a logistics hub for trafficking, and has lost its status as one of the safest countries in Central America.
Fernandez, who took office in May, campaigned on a promise to crack down on the crime wave, and said she is drawing inspiration from El Salvador's iron-fisted President Nayib Bukele.

Attorney General Carlo Diaz announced an investigation into the murder, adding that Rodriguez – who had contributed to various Costa Rican print, radio and television media outlets and more recently turned to social media – had declined to enter a witness protection programme.
8faeb6764a33b86a: LONDON: Britain needs a "complete system reset" of welfare benefits and employment support for young people to lower its rate of youth inactivity from one of the highest in Europe, according to a major report which will be published in full on Tuesday.

Alan Milburn, a former minister from prime minister Andy Burnham's Labour Party, will propose lower benefit payments for Britons aged under 25 and more mandatory work placements for the long-term youth unemployed.
The government has supported the review and Burnham has spoken of the need to act on its findings.

"A complete system reset is needed," Milburn said in remarks ahead of the release of the full government-commissioned report, due at 1130 GMT. "It is time for a new settlement that makes work not welfare the future for the next generation," he said.

Britain had 981,000 people aged 16-24 not in employment, education or training (NEET) in the second quarter of this year, accounting for one in eight of the age group and a share that was the second-highest in Europe last year.

Its 15.6% youth unemployment rate is also unusually high relative to the 3.4% rate for older workers — elsewhere in Europe, the youth jobless rate is typically only just over double that of older age groups.

Milburn said his proposals would aim to lower the NEET rate to 5% over a 10-year period through a mix of stronger employer incentives, better mental health support and a doubling of the number of young people studying for apprenticeships.

Any cuts to welfare are likely to concern many Labour lawmakers, who largely thwarted attempts to tighten eligibility rules under Burnham's predecessor Keir Starmer, handing ammunition to their political opponents who accuse the party of being on the side of welfare claimants, not workers.

The full version of the report is likely to be closely scrutinised for how much up-front spending it recommends and how soon it will deliver savings, at a time when some investors have said the government has failed to control welfare spending.
Britain spends around £8 billion (US$11 billion) a year on its main disability and unemployment benefits for people aged 18-24, while spending on back-to-work measures has fallen since 2010.
Milburn said he wants the balance between youth benefits spending and measures to support young people into work or education to shift from 25-to-1 to 2-to-1.

Employers said the government needed to ensure it made economic sense to hire inexperienced workers — especially as Britain's minimum wage is higher relative to average earnings than in almost all other rich economies.

"Businesses want to give young people opportunities. But too often they are arriving in the jobs market with little workplace experience, while the costs and risks of taking them on continue to rise," said Shevaun Haviland, director general of the British Chambers of Commerce.

29db87aa2b04d843: SHAH ALAM: A husband and wife claimed trial at the sessions court here today to accepting deposits from the public without a valid government licence.
Azrainuddin Zainal, who runs a programming business, and Nur Ezdiani Baharoddin face two charges each under Section 137 of the Financial Services Act.

They are accused of accepting deposits from the public through an investment scheme, Dinar Dirham, which involved purchasing and handling the digital currency DinarCoin, without a Bank Negara Malaysia licence.
The offences allegedly took place at a shop unit in Jalan Prima SG2, Prima Sri Gombak, in Gombak, between January 2016 and November 2017.
If found guilty under Section 137 of the Act, Azrainuddin and Ezdiani face up to 10 years in prison or a maximum fine of RM50 million.
Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud granted Azrainuddin and Ezdiani bail of RM30,000 with one surety each.
He also ordered them to surrender their passports to the court pending the disposal of their case, and to refrain from interfering with potential witnesses.
The court set Jan 20 for case management.

Deputy public prosecutor Nurdeenie Rashid and prosecuting officer Alya Hazira Kassim appeared for the prosecution while Azrainuddin and Ezdiani were represented by lawyers Fudhail Ahmad Zulaini and Arif Imran Jahaberdeen.

5fa3cb1db2febb61: PETALING JAYA: An Umno leader has warned against mistaking Barisan Nasional's (BN) commanding victories in the Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka polls as the party regaining the acceptance of voters nationwide.

Kedah Umno information chief Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin said the victories must be assessed in light of the factors influencing voters' decisions, including the long-awaited Malay unity pact with PAS.

Shaiful, the Merbok Umno chief, said public dissatisfaction with Pakatan Harapan's performance in Putrajaya was another factor that would have prompted voters to send a message in the three state elections.
"People may have wanted to vent their frustration by sending a message in the three state elections that have taken place," he said on the Bincang Naratif podcast.
"What worries me most is that sometimes our leaders win in consecutive elections and (then) assume that public support has returned to us, that the people have begun to miss us again.
"I don't think that is accurate," he said.
Shaiful urged party leaders not to regard the state election results as a measure of public support or become overly confident ahead of the 16th general election.
"That is a very dangerous position to take. State election results cannot be used as a basis or benchmark for general elections."
At the Johor election on July 11, BN secured a landslide victory by winning 48 of the 56 state seats, up from 40 in 2022.
In the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan polls, BN formed a pact with PAS-led Perikatan Nasional and romped to a two-thirds majority, with BN taking 18 seats and PN seven.
Most recently, at the Melaka polls last weekend, BN retained 21 seats while PN secured three, giving the alliance a two-thirds majority in yet another state.
4ed73522589261bd: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — A White Paper on Malaysia’s preparations to become an aged nation is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Dec 2, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said.
He said Malaysia entered ageing-nation status in 2021 and is expected to become an aged nation by 2048 before reaching super-aged status in 2060.

He said plans for this demographic shift should not be viewed solely through the lens of managing senior citizens’ welfare, but must also include equipping future generations for structural changes in the economy and society.

“Preparations for becoming an aged nation are not merely about identifying existing gaps that need to be improved, but also about preparing future generations to face this situation,” he said at the Economy Ministry’s monthly assembly today. Also present was Deputy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah.

He noted that Malaysia’s transition from an ageing nation to an aged nation will be relatively brief, about 27 years, necessitating early groundwork to ensure the demographic shift does not create a generational divide.

Future changes in population and workforce numbers will also affect the country’s economic capacity, including the need to ensure that senior citizens can sustain their livelihoods as well as remain capable of contributing to society and the economy, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
In addition, he said the government is also examining the economic potential that can be unlocked from the demographic shift, including through the silver economy concept.

He said areas that will be given attention include job opportunities for senior citizens, ageing-related economic opportunities, the care economy, and efforts to make communities and cities more age-friendly.
“How we create economic opportunities and potential is tied to these changing dynamics. In terms of theme, we are indeed adopting the silver economy,” he said.

The silver economy refers to a market system of products and services designed specifically to meet the needs, wants and purchasing power of senior citizens and retirees, in line with Malaysia’s transition towards ageing-nation status.
Senior citizens’ welfare and care should not be viewed as a zero-sum game but must instead be assessed in terms of the benefits it can deliver to the country and to families, he said.
Improving the welfare of senior citizens has the potential to generate returns for the national economy if supported by appropriate structures and systems, he said.
At the same time, investment in the younger generation must remain a priority and form part of the nation’s preparations for demographic change, he added.
“Investment in the younger generation cannot be sidelined; it must serve as the foundation for preparing ourselves for an aged nation,” he said.
He said the White Paper will examine the issue more comprehensively before the government rolls out a full blueprint for addressing an aged nation thereafter.

He said population ageing transcends political and generational interests, as it is tied to Malaysia’s ability to strike a balance between demographic change and the country’s economic needs. — Bernama
0e7775eb4b53dba8: KUALA LUMPUR: The REDtone Kuala Lumpur International Junior Championships is growing stronger by bringing together 970 aspiring young squash players from 22 countries for its 18th edition.

The championships on Dec 1-6 continue to provide an important platform for young athletes to showcase their abilities, compete against international peers and gain valuable experience in their sporting journeys.
Of the 970 participants, 677 are from Malaysia, while 293 are international players.
Singapore leads the overseas contingent with 67 participants, followed by Hong Kong (51), South Korea (27) and Sri Lanka (20).
The championship continues to uphold its Platinum status for the eighth year since 2017.
It is recognised as the biggest junior squash event in Asia and the second-biggest in the world after the US Junior Open.
The tournament will be hosted across three venues at the National Sports Council (NSC) Squash Centre in Jalan Duta, Universiti Malaya Squash Courts and Astaka Squash Courts in Petaling Jaya.
The competition will feature six age categories each in the boys' and girls' divisions - Under-9, Under-11, Under-13, Under-15, Under-17 and Under-19.
All finals and third-and-fourth-place matches will be held at the Jalan Duta Squash Courts.
REDtone Group Chief Executive Officer, Lau Bik Soon, said the company's involvement goes beyond supporting a sporting event, reflecting its belief in creating opportunities for the next generation.
"As REDtone celebrates 30 years of growth and progress, we remain committed to supporting initiatives that create meaningful opportunities and make a positive impact on the community," he said.

Bik Soon also commended the Squash Rackets Association of Federal Territory Kuala Lumpur (SRAFTKL) for its dedication and efforts in organising the championship and contributing to the development of squash in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, SRAFTKL president and organising chairman Steven Kwan said the championship's continued growth and international recognition reflected the dedication of the association and its partners.

"The championship provides an important platform for young players to test their abilities against international competition, gain valuable experience and further develop their potential. We look forward to welcoming players from across the world for another exciting edition," he said.
4b2d15ce2a9b5074: WASHINGTON: US billionaire Warren Buffett has donated shares in his investment firm Berkshire Hathaway for a total of US$5.5 billion to charitable organisations run by his children, the company announced.

"Today, Warren E. Buffett, Chairman Emeritus, will convert 6,150 Class A shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares and will donate these shares to four family foundations: 3,690,000 shares to The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation and 1,845,000 shares to each of The Sherwood Foundation, The Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and NoVo Foundation," Berkshire Hathaway said in a statement, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
At the market close, the price per share was US$592.85, bringing the total value of the donation to approximately US$5.47 billion.

Each of Buffett's children already manages their own philanthropic initiatives. Susan Buffett focuses on education, Howard Buffett works on combating hunger and providing aid to those affected by conflict, and Peter Buffett supports local communities. All three intend to distribute the funds during their own lifetimes, though they are not yet certain whether they will be able to do so.

Warren Buffett became a billionaire in 1986, having transformed the investment holding company Berkshire Hathaway into a massive corporation through a strategy of value investing. He currently ranks as one of the ten wealthiest people in the world.
6c22de9658740de2: KUALA LUMPUR: Eighty-five localities covered by the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in the interiors of Sarawak have been affected after the service was temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in September.
The Health Ministry said, of that number, 16 localities were identified as having no access via alternative land and water transport.

"The ministry temporarily suspended FDS operations to allow a full investigation and assessment of the service's safety and operational aspects," it said in a written reply posted on Parliament's official website.

It was responding to a question from Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok), who asked for details on the number of areas affected by the temporary halt of the FDS in interior Sarawak, the alternatives provided, and the maximum period for patients to obtain treatment in emergencies.

To reduce the impact on affected communities, the ministry said several measures have been taken to ensure service continuity through the optimisation of land and water routes and the activation of referral and alternative transport mechanisms.
Priority is given to localities based on clinical risk, degree of remoteness and the availability of alternative access, the ministry said.

For emergency cases during this temporary suspension, the ministry said it ensures every patient receives immediate action based on clinical priority through the emergency medical evacuation (Medevac) service or suitable alternative transport.

To that end, the ministry is working with the Fire and Rescue Department and other agencies to help manage emergency cases and ensure continuity of access to emergency treatment for interior residents, taking into account weather conditions, road conditions, asset availability and operational safety.
On Sept 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
160477b3199cb1bf: WASHINGTON: US air travel returned to near-normal on Monday after a rare no-takeoff order left travellers stranded on airport floors from coast to coast over the weekend.
At least 350 flights into, out of, or within the US were cancelled Monday, according to tracker FlightAware, far fewer than the 9,200 cancelled when the ground stop order was handed down on Friday.

As he departed for a trip to China earlier Monday, president Donald Trump blamed "old equipment, broken equipment" and the previous administration for a communications failure that saw federal aviation authorities halt takeoffs nationwide for only the second time since the 9/11 attacks.
"We've been trying to get the money for two years to fix it," Trump told reporters, punting the problem to Congress.

The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that old networking equipment in Arkansas - and possibly in Texas - became overloaded, creating a communications failure that cascaded across 17 of the nation's 22 major air control centres.

It was the longest nationwide halt to takeoffs since 9/11, and the cancelations rippled through the industry, with planes stranded at airports where they were not needed and crews reaching limits on how long they could work.
United Airlines separately reported a widespread outage on Monday that briefly delayed departures before it was resolved.
The Trump administration has been at pains to say during Friday's ground stop that there was no threat to safety and that the disruption was not the result of a cyberattack.

Instead, it was "an old system that went down, and went down everywhere" after "it got overloaded," transportation secretary Sean Duffy said Friday night, before rebuffing calls for his resignation over the weekend.
Earlier in the week, Duffy had asked Congress for more than US$30 billion to upgrade and modernise the US air traffic control system.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said "we implemented a nationwide ground stop out of an abundance of caution" and that "throughout the disruption, certain radio frequencies and radar feeds remained operational, allowing air traffic controllers to maintain communication with and track aircraft."

The nationwide halt was lifted at 8.15pm Friday after about four hours, but untangling the mess of mislocated planes and personnel - and thousands of passengers who needed to be rebooked - continued into Monday.

Duffy upped his appeal to US lawmakers for additional funding late Friday, saying he needed US$50 billion to upgrade and modernise the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the government's purse strings, to provide the money.
"This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding," Duffy said at the White House. "This is bipartisan. This is American. I want US$50 billion."
The last major outage, in January 2023, saw all US departures halted after a different system, the Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) communications network, malfunctioned.
In that case, the FAA blamed software rather than hardware, saying a "damaged database file" was likely the cause. The takeoff halt lasted just under two hours.
6e0bc358d6eb6c60: SEREMBAN: The High Court has ordered the four disputed undangs and two other nobles to be present in court when two contempt proceedings against them are heard in a dispute concerning the Negeri Sembilan royal crisis.

Justice Roz Mawar Rozain issued the directive after granting leave to the state's royal court, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, to initiate a second set of contempt proceedings against the six.
"Your clients must be present as this is a quasi-criminal case," she said, fixing Dec 15 for the hearing.

The six are former Sungai Ujong undang Mubarak Dohak; former Jelebu undang Maarof Mat Rashad; former Rembau undang Abdul Rahim Yasin; Johol undang Muhammed Abdullah; the Tunku Besar of Tampin, Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri; and former Sungai Ujong shahbandar Badarudin Abdul Khalid.

The second contempt proceedings concern allegations that the six evaded service of court papers after Roz Mawar granted the DKU and Raja Norazli leave to initiate the first committal proceedings against them on July 8.
The dispute began on May 5, when Mubarak and five others filed an originating summons seeking a copy of the minutes of a special DKU meeting held on April 17.
The minutes recorded a decision to remove Mubarak as the Sungai Ujong undang.

On June 5, the High Court granted an ad interim injunction to preserve the status quo, including the existing composition of the DKU and Raja Norazli's position as its secretary, pending the determination of questions concerning jurisdiction and justiciability.

Raja Norazli subsequently claimed that media reports showed the plaintiffs, particularly Maarof, had been involved in the purported appointment of a "new" Yang Dipertuan Besar under Article 11 of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, despite the injunction remaining in force.
The DKU and Raja Norazli subsequently obtained leave to commence committal proceedings against the six.
On July 8, Roz Mawar found a prima facie case of contempt and ordered the six to answer the allegations.
Last week, the Court of Appeal dismissed applications by the six to stay the first contempt proceedings.

A three-member panel said the applicants failed to approach the court with clean hands, citing their failure to make full and frank disclosure of other proceedings filed outside the High Court in Seremban.
Steven Thiru, Shafrin Halim, David Matthew, Gregory Das and Gurjeevan Singh Sachdev appeared for the DKU and Raja Norazli in today's proceedings.
Zainuddin Omar represented the Tunku Besar of Tampin, while Asmawi Ismail and Deidra Nur Azmi appeared for the remaining five.
8ed767dc21e77a4b: KUALA LUMPUR: FMT Media Sdn Bhd executive chairman Nelson Fernandez received the Global Captains of Industry Award at the 2026 International CEO and Business Leaders Forum here today.

Presented during the forum’s opening ceremony at Berjaya Times Square Hotel, the award is among KSI Strategic Institute for Asia Pacific's honours recognising business leaders for their contributions to the Malaysian and global economy.

The 2026 International CEO and Business Leaders Forum brings together business leaders and industry experts to discuss how companies can remain competitive and grow amid geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

Fernandez is scheduled to speak at the forum’s afternoon panel on building lasting businesses through stronger resilience, competitiveness and growth.

9a20ddbfe09e08d9: LOS ANGELES: California on Monday filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the artificial intelligence company endangered the public when its agents went rogue and hacked a platform known as Hugging Face.

The lawsuit from California attorney general Rob Bonta was filed in San Francisco Superior Court and alleges OpenAI knowingly developed and tested its experimental technology "without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect the public."
The 31-page filing refers to a July 2026 incident where experimental versions of OpenAI's models "accessed the public internet and launched a cyberattack on Hugging Face," an AI platform.

"The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritises growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability - and this was only one of 80 known incidents," Bonta said in a statement.
"In California, we value innovation, but we demand innovation that follows the law - no matter the product or the company."

The lawsuit alleges OpenAI is in violation of state laws for "deficient safety procedures, disregard for public safety and the known testing of a dangerous product without oversight, as well as its misleading statements to consumers and the public."
OpenAI spokesman Drew Pusateri said the company has "undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity," in a statement to US media.
"This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab," Pusateri added.
The California lawsuit is the latest legal woe faced by the tech innovator.
British Columbia has sued OpenAI over a mass school shooting in the Western Canadian province, where it's alleged the company failed to report violent activity on its ChatGPT service by the shooter.
5c13a5a350f11954: TOKYO, Nov 17 — It’s censored in Japan, not officially sold in China, and has floundered in Asian markets where mobile games are king, but Grand Theft Auto fever is sweeping the continent regardless.

Excitement among gamers in Asia for Thursday’s GTA VI mega-release shows how the industry has evolved since the fifth instalment in 2013, and quashes the idea that cultural aversion to lawless escapades holds it back, analysts say.
“The game was part of my youth,” Yang Hauiyu, a market research professional in Beijing, told AFP, recalling playing a pirated PC version non-stop as a teen.
Like others worldwide, Yang, now in his 30s, pre-downloaded GTA VI for his PlayStation — even though the video game is not licensed for sale in mainland China.
Playing GTA is not banned, but as with most Western-made games, the series, notorious for its violent scenarios, has never obtained government approval.
However, a large grey market for GTA exists in the world’s second-largest economy.
Fans access it via servers in Hong Kong and elsewhere while authorities turn a blind eye, even as the series’ popularity balloons, said Shenzhen-based gaming consultant Daniel Camilo.
“The console market was minuscule in China and now it’s much bigger,” he said, adding that the middle class has grown since 2013 and younger gamers are more open to global pop culture.

Camilo predicted “GTA VI” could be the first GTA game with a significant commercial impact from China — the country with the globe’s highest gaming revenues, according to industry analysis firm Newzoo.
He estimated sales of two to five million copies from the nation, a figure which is “virtually impossible to track”.
Z-rated
In Thailand, where GTA sales were suspended in 2008 after an alleged copycat murder of a taxi driver, one Bangkok gaming centre is now advertising “GTA VI” sessions from launch day.
But for some, the heavily American themes in the US-published series are off-putting.
Donghwi Kim, a 23-year-old South Korean student, is a big fan of Nintendo’s Zelda games, but has not tried GTA.
“It’s focused on the United States’ culture, right?” he said. “I don’t have interest in that”.
In Japan, home of the PlayStation, GTA V was the seventh top-selling game in the 2013-14 financial year, below six Japanese-made rivals, gaming magazine Famitsu reported.
In contrast, “GTA V” was the “best-selling console video game of 2013 in North America, Latin America and Europe combined”, its publisher said at the time.
The game is censored on consoles in Japan to comply with strict explicit-content rules that refuse to classify works depicting genitals, sexual acts or prostitution in a positive light.
To obtain a “Z-rated” — adult-only — classification, Japan’s GTA V replaces a sexual act with smoking a cigarette, shows strippers with their breasts covered, and cuts torture scenes short.
Although nothing is yet confirmed, censorship rumours were fuelled for GTA VI because the Japanese version is around a gigabyte smaller than the international one.
‘Enormous’ anticipation
For Indian players used to navigating chaotic traffic, overloaded motorbikes and daredevil overtaking, the game’s high-speed chases hold a particular appeal.
India’s gaming market generated US$2.7 billion (RM11.04 billion) in 2024, and more than half a billion people played in the past year, according to separate government and industry figures.
But more than 90 per cent of Indian gamers use mobile phones — making the console-owning audience for a blockbuster such as “GTA VI” a much smaller, more affluent group.

Indian fans are celebrating the launch with gaming marathons and unofficial parties, including a Vice City-inspired night in tech hub Chennai featuring virtual-reality gaming, superbikes and live graffiti.
“The anticipation is enormous,” said party organiser Fahad Saud, 35, who grew up playing GTA’s multiple editions.
“In India, where the day-to-day struggle is so great, GTA gives us the avenue to vent the pressure, to have space and freedom.”
PC vs console

“GTA has historically had a smaller share of the overall gaming market in many Asian countries compared to North America and Europe,” said Daniel Ahmad, director of research and insights at Niko Partners.
But its popularity “is driven more by differences in gaming platforms, business models, and spending habits than cultural preferences”, he told AFP.
The high cost is a barrier, and at launch “GTA VI” is only coming to consoles — a gadget that plays a smaller role in many Asian markets.
“We expect the launch to generate significantly greater attention in Asia than previous entries in the franchise,” Ahmad said.
However, “much of the fanfare will be reserved for the PC launch, given the larger PC gaming audience”.
Indonesian Jonathan Nainggolan, 34, asked his wife’s permission to purchase the game’s “ultimate edition”, which costs around US$80 in the country.
“I expect to play the game continuously… probably, until the end of the year, I will try to complete GTA VI.” — AFP
0d0dd399016343e1: PETALING JAYA: Istana Negeri Sembilan masih belum mengesahkan peletakan jawatan Adun Juasseh Ismail Lasim sebagai menteri besar, meskipun perkara itu diumumkan Barisan Nasional (BN) malam tadi.

Pengelola Bijaya Diraja memaklumkan surat peletakan jawatan itu hanya dihantar ke Istana Hinggap di Seremban pada 12.16 tengah malam tadi oleh seorang individu bernama Hamidi, yang mendakwa mewakili firma guaman Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq.
Menurutnya, peletakan jawatan Ismail perlu dikemukakan kepada Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan dan hanya berkuat kuasa selepas mendapat perkenan baginda.
Beliau turut mendedahkan bahawa Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir telah bersetuju untuk menerima menghadap Ismail dan pemimpin Umno itu dimaklumkan mengenainya pada 8.38 malam tadi.
“Sesi menghadap ditetapkan pada 10 pagi Jumaat (20 Nov).

d86902990ce4f487: CHICAGO: United Airlines said on Monday it had resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures for about an hour, just days after a nationwide air traffic control outage caused widespread disruption to US airlines.
The disruption, which ended around 6 pm ET, highlighted how computer failures can ground flights even when aircraft and crews are ready to depart.

There was no indication that United's outage was connected to Friday's Federal Aviation Administration shutdown, which caused the longest nationwide ground stop of departing flights since the Sept 11, 2001, attacks on the US.
"This is not an FAA system-wide problem," US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in an interview on Monday on Fox News' "Hannity" show. "I don't know what the root cause of United is," he added.
United said a technology issue that delayed flight departures had been resolved, adding that flights already airborne and those operated by United Express had been unaffected throughout.
"There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue," the airline said.
An internal memo from United's pilots union, seen by Reuters, said a companywide web-based outage had affected multiple applications used by pilots, including crew communications.

The memo said United had been unable to provide final aircraft weights for departing flights and advised pilots to follow airport station guidance on whether to leave their gates. Such information is essential for pilots to complete pre-departure calculations.
In a subsequent memo, the union said United's systems were coming back online and directed pilots to check updated company communications.

Airlines have experienced similar disruptions before. In August 2025, United temporarily grounded flights after a problem with its Unimatic system, which supplies flight information to systems used to calculate aircraft weight and balance. It was not immediately clear whether Monday's outage involved United's Unimatic system.
Alaska Airlines also briefly halted departures nationwide in April 2024 after a problem with its weight-and-balance system.

As of 6:50 pm ET, United had delayed 645 flights, or 20% of its schedule, and canceled 25 on Monday, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware. It was unclear how many of those disruptions were caused by Monday's technology issue, as airlines were still recovering from Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop.
United shares went down 2.5% in after-hours trading.
Some passengers reported on social media that their aircraft had returned to the gate after reaching the runway.
The outage came as US air travel was largely returning to normal following Friday's nationwide ground stop, which lasted nearly five hours after a failure in the FAA's telecommunications network.

More than 18,100 flights scheduled to depart US airports between Friday and Sunday were canceled or had not taken off within three hours of their scheduled departure times, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. Not all were necessarily affected by the FAA outage.
09e59365d3520a00: LANGKAWI: The fastest Malaysian male finishers from the past three editions of Ironman Malaysia will line up together on Nov 21, with an experienced women's field joining the pursuit of the fastest Malaysian triathlete honours.
Hafiz Yusup, last year's fastest Malaysian male, joins Fawwaz Fauzi and Azmir Taib, who achieved the distinction in 2024 and 2023, respectively.
Last year's second-fastest Malaysian male, Nur Radzman Munib, is also entered for the full-distance race.
The women's field features Ann Pow, the fastest Malaysian female in 2022 and 2024, alongside Yen Chia, Mimi Ruslan, Aimi Iwasaki and Nursyahariah Jusoh.
Chew Huey Ming, the fastest Malaysian female at last year's Ironman 70.3 Langkawi, is also registered for the full-distance triathlon.
The Malaysian contests form part of a Nov 19–22 race week which will bring together 1,900 athletes from 65 countries. Both Ironman Malaysia and Ironman 70.3 Langkawi take place on November 21.
Ironman athletes will take on a 3.8km swim, 180km cycle and 42.2km run.
Hafiz returns after recording 10:52:02 to finish as the fastest Malaysian male last year despite suffering from influenza a week before the race.
That performance followed second-fastest Malaysian finishes in 2019, 2023 and 2024, and third-fastest in 2022.

"This year, I'm not putting pressure on myself to retain that honour. My main aim is to perform better than last year. I have a personal target, but what matters more to me is seeing what I can achieve during the race," said Hafiz.
In the women's contest, Ann brings two previous fastest Malaysian finishes, having completed the full distance in 11:55:44 in 2022 and 11:33:41 in 2024.

Chia adds a consistent challenger across both distances. She was the third-fastest Malaysian female in the full race in 2023 with 12:56:54 and again in 2024 with 12:19:27, before finishing third-fastest in last year's 70.3 event in 5:37:06.
She returns to the full distance following a fourth-place finish in the women's 35–39 age group at Ironman Vietnam earlier this year in 11:16:07.
"I feel good about my training so far, so I hope I can perform well this Saturday," said Chia, who will be making her fourth Ironman Malaysia appearance.
At Ironman 70.3 Langkawi, Afiq Syazwan Shahru features among the Malaysian male contenders alongside Yap Qi Yi, Edwin Thiang and Danish Affan Hasnul Basri.

Afiq progressed from third-fastest Malaysian male in 2024 to second-fastest last year in 4:46:59. Qi Yi was the fastest Malaysian male in 2024 with 4:45:10, while Edwin finished third-fastest in 2025 in 5:01:53.
Danish is registered for the half distance after finishing as the third-fastest Malaysian male in the 2023 full race.

The women's Ironman 70.3 entries include Lynn Guan, the third-fastest Malaysian female in the 2018 edition, and former national cyclist and duathlete Mariana Mohammad. Harum Delima is also registered after completing last year's full-distance race.
The Ironman 70.3 event comprises a 1.9km swim, 90km cycle and 21.1km run, with approximately 969 metres of elevation gain on this year's cycling course.
The event is supported by the Langkawi Development Authority and the Malaysia Convention & Exhibition Bureau (MyCEB), an agency under the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry.

8d362f1a08f6f8b7: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite a softening property market and concerns over oversupply in Kuala Lumpur, Paramount Corp Bhd remains confident in the resilience of the city's high-end residential segment, underpinned by rising regional wealth, stronger foreign buyer interest and growing demand for larger homes in prime urban locations.

While the oversupply situation in Kuala Lumpur, particularly around the KLCC area, has become slightly more pronounced in 2026, Paramount believes the market needs to be viewed through a more differentiated lens.

Not all segments are facing the same challenges, with the bulk of the existing overhang concentrated in different product categories from the premium residential market that the group is targeting, Paramount Group chief executive officer Jeffrey Chew told Business Times.
He said the company takes a highly research-driven approach before embarking on any development, carefully assessing the underlying demand and buyer profile for each project.

"What we are seeing is that, over the last 18 months, interest from foreign buyers in Malaysia has grown quite substantially. At the same time, wealth creation across Southeast Asia and the wider Asian region has been tremendous.

"This has created an increasingly affluent buyer pool, with more people moving up from the middle-market segment into higher-end properties. They are searching for larger homes, better specifications and more prestigious urban addresses.
"While there is an oversupply in certain segments, we believe the demand for well-located, premium residential properties remains strong," he said.
Paramount's confidence is supported by the performance of its Ashwood development, which has demonstrated the depth of demand for larger, high-end residences in Kuala Lumpur.
The project, which is currently under construction, was fully sold within 18 months of its launch in 2024, with units priced between RM1.5 million and RM4.3 million.
Notably, about 70 per cent of its buyers were foreigners, coming from markets including China, Taiwan, Japan, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.
The development attracted buyers seeking larger living spaces, with built-up areas ranging from about 1,500 sq ft to 4,000 sq ft.

Chew said the response to Ashwood reinforced the group's view that there remains a distinct market for premium homes, particularly among affluent international buyers who value location, space and quality.
The project is expected to be completed in 2028.
"We were very encouraged by the response to Ashwood. It demonstrated that there is still a sizeable market for larger, premium residential units, particularly among foreign buyers.
"That gives us confidence as we move forward with The Ashbourne, where we expect to see a similar profile of buyers," he said.
Paramount is now looking to build on that success through The Ashbourne, its RM1.3 billion residential development and its third project in the prestigious U-Thant enclave of Kuala Lumpur.

The development will comprise two towers housing 458 high-end serviced residences, with built-up areas ranging from 1,491 sq ft to 2,661 sq ft. Prices will range from RM1.8 million to slightly above RM4 million per unit, or about RM1,350 per sq ft.
Chew acknowledged that market conditions have become more challenging since the launch of Ashwood in 2024, with the property market showing signs of softening in 2026.

This has prompted the group to take a more cautious view of buyer demand, particularly regarding whether foreign purchasers would maintain their interest and whether domestic buyers could provide sufficient depth to absorb the new supply.
Nevertheless, he believes The Ashbourne is well-positioned to capture demand from the premium market.

"We are conscious that the market has softened somewhat. Naturally, we have to consider whether foreign buyers will continue to come into the market and whether local buyers will be able to absorb the supply.
"But we remain cautiously confident. Construction and material costs have increased significantly over the years, and the trend has also influenced the pricing of new developments.
"We have started our pre-registration exercise, and the initial response has been encouraging. We believe The Ashbourne can attract a fairly positive response," he said.
The project is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2030.

He said beyond the development itself, Paramount's partnership with Japan's Mitsui Fudosan represents a strategic step in strengthening its international profile and expanding its reach among overseas property buyers.

Under the joint venture, Mitsui Fudosan (Asia) Malaysia Sdn Bhd will acquire a 49 per cent equity interest in Meridian Kuasa Sdn Bhd for RM23.1 million, while Paramount retains a controlling 51 per cent stake.
Meridian Kuasa will serve as the development vehicle for The Ashbourne, with Paramount leading project management, sales and marketing.

Chew said Paramount had deliberately sought a strong international partner, recognising that securing a prestigious development site alone would not be enough to establish its presence in the global residential market.
"Mitsui Fudosan is a major international property player with an established presence in malls, commercial assets and high-rise developments.
"We knew that if we wanted to attract a partner of this calibre, we had to secure a very good piece of land with strong development potential.
"One of our objectives when acquiring the land was to take our brand beyond Malaysia. We believe Mitsui Fudosan is the right partner because of its strong international reputation.
"When we market the development overseas, having a recognised international name alongside Paramount will help strengthen buyers' confidence in our product," he said.
The partnership also provides a platform for potential future collaboration, bringing together Mitsui Fudosan's international experience and market reach with Paramount's local development expertise.
Despite its growing focus on premium developments, Chew stressed that Paramount was not abandoning its traditional role as a people's developer.
The group will continue to cater to the needs of Malaysian homebuyers while expanding its portfolio to address the changing aspirations of a more affluent regional buyer base.
He said the strategy was not about moving away from the group's core market but rather responding to the evolution of wealth and purchasing power across Malaysia and the wider region.
"We are still very much the people's developers. Internally, that remains our philosophy. We want to meet the housing needs of people, both in Malaysia and overseas.

"At the same time, we recognise that wealth across Southeast Asia and Asia has grown significantly. Buyers' aspirations have evolved, and there is a growing segment looking for larger homes, premium products and more affluent locations.
"We want to participate in that growth, but we are certainly not abandoning our bread-and-butter business," he said.
Meanwhile, Paramount said in a statement today that it has appointed branding agency IMAJEN to develop the brand strategy and creative positioning for The Ashbourne.
Evon Chong, co-founder of IMAJEN, said the projects that matter most to developers usually carry an ambition to move the brand forward," he said.
"Visionary developers are rarely looking to repeat what has already been done, even when it has been successful," he said.

0ba7a28a7106c0ec: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 5,332 of the 5,986 private health facilities and community pharmacies monitored have started displaying medicine prices, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad told the Dewan Rakyat.
The figure represents 89.1 per cent of the premises monitored by the Health Ministry between May 2025 and September 2026, he said.
Of the total, 3,905 premises (65.2 per cent) achieved a satisfactory level of price display, while 649 (10.8 per cent) had yet to display medicine prices.
Dzulkefly said this in a written parliamentary reply to Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) yesterday.
Tan had asked about the compliance rate and findings since the policy took effect, as well as its impact on transparency, healthy competition and medicine prices for patients.
Community pharmacies recorded the highest satisfactory rate at 73.1 per cent, involving 2,628 of 3,595 premises.
Private hospitals followed at 61.4 per cent (78 of 127), while private medical clinics recorded 57.2 per cent (972 of 1,699).
Dental clinics had the lowest rate at 43.6 per cent (219 of 502).
Mandatory medicine price display took effect on May 1, 2025, under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Medicines) Order 2025.
Several medical and dental practitioner associations filed for a judicial review of the requirement in July last year.

772ddf7428207166: TAIPEI: The timing of Washington's US$14 billion arms sales package to Taiwan is "very much up to" President Donald Trump and will not be affected by the US midterm results, according to a Taiwanese government official.
Taiwan has been waiting months for Trump to approve the record sale of weapons and equipment that the island says it needs to strengthen its defence capabilities to deter a potential Chinese attack.
Beijing claims the island democracy is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
Trump has stalled the arms sale, saying in May it could be used as a bargaining chip with China, as the two superpowers tried to ease trade tensions.
"When it comes to time, I think it's very much up to... President Trump," said Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi.
Taiwan enjoys "very strong bipartisan support" from Congress, and this month's midterm results, which saw Democrats win control of the House and Senate, would not affect the timing, Chen said.
The Trump administration had to consider "many factors" when it came to arms sales to Taiwan, including the Middle East war.
"We respect that, but at the same time, we express that we really have an urgent need for those capabilities," Chen said.
Patriot missiles, an automated command and control system and a 360-degree air defence radar system are among the items in the US$14 billion package.
Chen said Taiwan had "very good direct communication" with the Trump administration and "we are reassured that that will not change".
"This could be just a matter of time before" the sale is approved, either as one package or in smaller parcels, he said.
Taiwan 'structurally important'
Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping for the third and fourth time this year at an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen this week and at the G20 in the United States in December.
While Taiwan has been on the agenda at previous talks between the rival leaders, Chen brushed off concerns about the upcoming meetings.
"We are very confident and very comfortable with our relationship with the US and with other like-minded partners," Chen said.
"We are structurally important, and our people (are) committed to our own defence. I think this (is) what matters the most," he said.
"And Taiwan stands in the middle of the whole AI revolution. I think that now almost every leader in the world understands the situation."
Taiwan is a powerhouse in the global semiconductor industry, producing nearly all of the most advanced chips for companies including Nvidia and Apple.

After Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who US intelligence agencies believe is spying for Beijing, Chen said the case underlines the need to be "very vigilant about China".
China is "very aggressive" when it comes to stealing intellectual property and technology to get around export controls, Chen said.
Huang, who regularly visited Taiwan to see Nvidia's clients, including TSMC, and had been seen in the capital Taipei with the Chinese woman, would be welcome back to the island, Chen said.
"He certainly will be welcome but I think... every business leader in the world has to learn this lesson that China is trying to poach your trade secrets," he said.
"They are going to arrange (a) spy in your life so that they can get easier access."
Beijing has rejected the allegations as "entirely baseless".
China is in a race for tech dominance against the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Taiwan has long accused China of carrying out espionage activities on the island, including targeting its tech sector.
