36ad406a443fa8c3: PETALING JAYA: The Negeri Sembilan palace has yet to verify Juasseh assemblyman Ismail Lasim’s resignation as menteri besar, despite the matter being announced by Barisan Nasional (BN) last night.

The comptroller of the Negeri Sembilan royal household said the supposed letter was only sent to Istana Hinggap in Seremban at 12.16am today by an individual named Hamidi, who said he was from the law firm Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq.
He said that under the state’s constitution, the menteri besar must submit his resignation to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, and that it only takes effect with the ruler's consent.
The comptroller also revealed that Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had agreed to grant Ismail an audience, saying the Umno leader was informed of this at 8.38pm last night.
Ismail reportedly sought an audience to express his loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz and seek the ruler’s consent for the state assembly to convene.
"Ismail also acknowledged the matter. The audience was fixed for 10am on Friday (Nov 20).
"The consent for the audience was given 80 minutes before BN secretary-general Zambry Abdul Kadir posted on Facebook about Ismail’s resignation as menteri besar.
"The palace has yet to verify the authenticity of the letter, which according to Zambry was signed by Ismail," the comptroller said in a statement.
Yesterday, Zambry said BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of Ismail’s resignation letter dated Nov 16, and that the coalition respected the Juasseh assemblyman’s decision.
Zambry said Zahid would propose a candidate for the menteri besar’s post to be presented to Tuanku Muhriz.
Negeri Sembilan has been embroiled in a royal crisis since April, when four purported undangs, or chieftains, announced Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
The same disputed undangs also purportedly proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the "new" ruler at a five-star hotel in Melaka in June.
Ismail initially recognised Tuanku Muhriz as ruler, but in September endorsed a statement issued by his executive council that purportedly affirmed Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
In response, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of the executive council members.
Ismail has since withdrawn a letter sent to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal concerning the purported removal of Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
98a26c6de0827b1a: TULKAREM: After Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast.
Prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed no return for the displaced people from the camp near the northern city of Jenin, known as a hub for militants.
He is now fighting for his political life after his party lost seats in Israel's general election last month and former general Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with trying to form a new government.
But even the prospect of an end to Netanyahu's rule is not enough to lift Darsieh's hopes.
"Whether it's this government or a new one, what does it change?" said the 64-year-old. "They're two sides of the same coin."

The Israeli military carried out a major operation in the north of the occupied Palestinian territory in early 2025, during a temporary ceasefire in Hamas-ruled Gaza, having vowed to root out extremists.
Shortly before the election, Netanyahu announced that no one removed from Tulkarem would be allowed back.

For Palestinian families, it is a second form of displacement. The Tulkarem camp was set up in 1950 for refugees who fled or were forced out during the creation of the state of Israel two years earlier. The West Bank has been occupied by Israel since 1967.

"Successive generations have lived through displacement without being able to return to their homes. If our grandparents and parents couldn't return, how can we believe that our return will be possible?" Darsieh said.
According to UN figures, the Israeli operation launched last year displaced 12,100 people from the Tulkarem camp.
'Empty stomachs'
With the Israeli military keeping up periodic operations around the region, Darsieh is living near the camp in a modest, makeshift home with a sheet metal roof. His wife uses a wheelchair.
He went to receive trays of mansaf, a dish of rice, meat and fermented yoghurt, prepared by Fazaa Kitchen, a solidarity group that serves food to the displaced.
Working from the building of the Wadi al-Hawarith charity, volunteers in orange jackets fill, seal and package portions of food in an assembly line.
The group prepares and distributes some 1,200 meals to 400 families.
"If we weren't cooking, families would be going to bed with empty stomachs," said the organisation's head, Hussein al-Sheikh Ali, 60, who himself is displaced.
He described Israel's actions in the West Bank since the Gaza war - a conflict launched in response to the unprecedented attack on Israel by Hamas on Oct 7, 2023 - as "collective punishment".
Netanyahu's now-caretaker government, which includes far-right figures, rapidly expanded Israeli settlements in the West Bank which are considered illegal under international law.
"Some Palestinians hope that a new Israeli government might emerge with a less extremist, more moderate tone," Ali said.
"Yet the fear remains that the same policies towards the Palestinians will persist, even if the political figures themselves change."
Faisal Salama, who heads Tulkarem camp's popular committee, which represents residents, called Netanyahu's decision to stop residents returning illegal.

But he held out guarded hope for an end to military operations. He pointed to how Israel, soon after the election, ended an operation in Hebron that displaced 3,000 Palestinians, which was launched after gunmen shot dead two Israeli soldiers.
'Scale of suffering'
Even if residents could return, much of the camp has been destroyed. Houses have been razed, buildings emptied and businesses burnt down.

Eisenkot, who commanded forces in the West Bank during the second Intifada, a Palestinian uprising from 2000 to 2005, has sought to appeal to a broad spectrum including liberals but has only taken some distance from Netanyahu on security.
Eisenkot backs the existence of the major settlements but has also spoken out forcefully against extremist settlers who have attacked Palestinians with virtual impunity.

Beth Oppenheim, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said a consensus has emerged among Jewish Israelis on key policies on the West Bank, including opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state.
Still, she said that Eisenkot as prime minister could be more flexible on allowing a return to Tulkarem.
"I think that given the political atmosphere in Israel today, this will be done through a security pretext," she said.
"They would make the case that this is necessary to stabilise the situation in the West Bank and that having people displaced could create the conditions for unrest," she said.
For Asia Assaf, 44, a Fazaa Kitchen volunteer whose home was destroyed in March 2025, political debates are far away from her daily concerns.
"One cannot truly grasp the scale of suffering until one has experienced it firsthand," she said.
84062266b7950328: PETALING JAYA: Keputusan PRN Melaka yang menyaksikan jurang undi Pakatan Harapan (PH) dengan gabungan Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) di lima DUN bawah Parlimen Kota Melaka mengecil kepada 5,479 undi, membuka ruang untuk ‘gelombang biru’ merampas kerusi itu pada PRU16.
Ketua Umno Kota Melaka, Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman, berkata PH memperoleh 56,455 undi di lima DUN itu, berbanding 50,976 dikumpulkan BN dan PN.
Katanya, perbezaan itu menunjukkan perubahan ketara berbanding PRU15 apabila calon PH bagi Parlimen Kota Melaka memperoleh majoriti 46,420 undi.
Parlimen Kota Melaka disandang Ketua DAP negeri, Khoo Poay Tiong sejak 2018.
Pada PRN 14 Nov lalu, PH memenangi tiga daripada lima kerusi berkenaan iaitu Kesidang, Kota Laksamana dan Bandar Hilir, manakala BN melalui Umno menawan Duyong dan Telok Mas.
Razak berkata, keputusan itu turut memperlihatkan keberkesanan pemindahan undi antara BN dan PN walaupun kerjasama kedua-dua gabungan dimeterai hanya beberapa hari sebelum penamaan calon.
Beliau berkata, kemenangan Umno di Duyong dan Telok Mas dengan majoriti melebihi 10,000 undi setiap DUN turut menjadi perkembangan penting dalam menilai perubahan sokongan pengundi di Parlimen itu.

“Perbandingan ini merupakan asas untuk meneliti perubahan landskap politik Kota Melaka, dengan mengambil kira kerjasama BN dan PN, calon dan parti yang diamanahkan untuk bertanding,” katanya di Facebook.
Razak berkata, keputusan di lima DUN itu wajar diberi perhatian oleh kepimpinan tertinggi Umno, BN dan PN dalam menentukan strategi serta pembahagian kerusi menjelang PRU16.
Beliau yang juga Adun Telok Mas berkata, jentera Umno Bahagian Kota Melaka akan terus diperkukuh bagi menghadapi PRU akan datang.

cee9982151e8e96e: SYDNEY: Australia said on Tuesday it will require tourists on working holiday visas to complete extra work in rural areas, as the government attempts to balance a reduction in migration with a shortage of labour in its farming and hospitality sectors.

Australia's Working Holiday Maker programme — a popular rite of passage for young people from more than a dozen countries — will now require applicants to complete four months of rural work to remain in the country for a second year, up from the current three months.
"Working holiday makers make an important contribution to our economy, especially in agriculture, tourism and hospitality and in regional Australia," Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said.
"But when demand grows too fast, the government needs the tools to manage the programme properly."
Rural employers in Australia are heavily reliant on backpackers to fill seasonal roles.
Under the programme for 18-to-35-year-olds, Australia grants a one-year working holiday visa, extendable for a second and third year if the backpackers undertake regional work.
Backpackers typically work as nannies, waiters and in farming, among other retail and hospitality jobs.

Under a 2021 carve-out agreed by previous governments in both countries, the rural work rules do not apply to UK backpackers, which has led to a surge of British arrivals in Australia and a shortage of workers in regional areas.

Australia has already announced curbs on foreign students bringing partners and children to accompany them while they study, as well as a ballot system for backpackers, amid growing debate in the country over high migration levels.
40443674f3bd5973: PARIS, (France): Cricket in France is at risk of disappearing altogether, less than two years before the sport makes its long-awaited Olympic return.
The last, and only time that cricket was played at the Olympics was in Paris in 1900, where England beat France by 158 runs to win the gold medal.

France will not be at the Twenty20 tournament at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, and cricket in the country is on the verge of "dying" due to a crisis within the country's federation, Miriam Romero, a player and administrator, told AFP.
Clubs suspended the national league this year as they try to force president Prebagarane 'Prebou' Balane to resign following a series of scandals.

The organisation lost its recognition by France's sports ministry early this year, while the International Cricket Council (ICC) in June suspended development funding and placed France Cricket on notice for "non-compliance with membership criteria."
This came after scandals such as 'ghost' women's matches and development funding that was unaccounted for.
"We must not let cricket die in France, it's a shame," Romero, who is president of the Paris regional cricket committee, told AFP.
"If we don't do anything (it will die)."
Romero, who at 65 still plays, was previously on France Cricket's finance committee and is also a director at Paris Universitaire Club (PUC), one of the main cricket clubs in France.
She says PUC and other clubs have left France Cricket and are trying to set up a new national association to replace the existing structure.
Others, though, simply want Balane to resign so they can resolve the governance issues that saw them lose recognition from the ICC and the sports ministry.
According to the minutes of a board meeting in June, seen by the France 24 television station before it was deleted from the France Cricket website, Balane said he would resign on July 17.
But board member Jubaid Ahamed said Balane had not fulfilled his promise.
Despite repeated attempts by AFP to contact Balane and France Cricket, neither replied.
The chaos led the main clubs in France Cricket's domestic championship to suspend the competition in mid-August, meaning the season was never completed.

They have had enough and their demands are simple: "Firstly, to change the president. Then, to restructure France Cricket by implementing more flexible rules to develop youth and women's cricket," Djega Sankaran, the former president of the Morangis club, south of Paris, said.
He said he had resigned so he could speak freely without repercussions for his club.

AFP spoke to the president of the France Gymkhana club, Rizwan Babri, the president of another club and the team manager from a third club who all confirmed they wanted Balane to resign and for France Cricket to be restructured.
One person described Balane as acting like "God Almighty", another accused him of treating the federation as "his private affair."

In November, 34 clubs — more than enough to reach the necessary one third threshold — asked France Cricket for an extraordinary general meeting to submit a motion of no confidence in Balane and the executive committee, but the president refused, in email responses seen by AFP.
- 'Cry-babies' -
The crisis had been brewing for some time.

It began when France 24 broke an explosive story in 2023 about clubs in the country faking women's matches, apparently so France Cricket could benefit from hundreds of thousands of dollars of ICC funding.
The national women's cricket team wrote an open letter demanding an investigation and accountability, but instead, France Cricket suspended them.
"What was sad for us was that the men, the other clubs, did not support us," Sabine Lieury, a former French women's international and ex-president of Nantes Cricket Club, told AFP.
"The cricket world didn't want to rebel with the French girls to say that this was unacceptable."
Worst of all, the men's national team accused the women of being "cry-babies" and disloyal.
"No one did anything, they kept playing to protect themselves."
But they changed their tune after France Cricket lost its ICC development funding and French government recognition.
France Cricket have always denied that women's ghost matches took place — Balane told the BBC in June that it had "never" happened.
But that was not true. In fact, it was still happening last year.
The problem was that the federation obliged clubs to set up a women's team and threatened them with fines or even demotion if they did not fulfil fixtures.
Some clubs tried, but there was not the necessary interest to do so in such a tight timeframe.

"Everyone brought women's teams one way or another, with cousins, but it was just to avoid Prebou's sanctions," said Sankaran, who was heavily involved in trying to develop cricket in the Ile de France region around Paris.
"There were six people here, four people there. There were no (real) matches."
In the end, it was easier not to have a women's team.
"There were agreements between clubs: 'You won't get a fine and I won't get a fine'. They made up the scores," said Sankaran.
"All the clubs made mistakes, me included."
- 'Not surprised' -
But those who were playing had always been suspicious.
There were four teams in the French women's first division at that time: Nantes, PUC, Lille and Lisses. But there were nine teams in the second division, and none were ever promoted.
"How is it that every year, we never see someone coming from these second division teams?" said Lieury.
"When the scandal broke, we were shocked, but at the same time, we said: 'we're not surprised, we've never seen these girls'."
Even in 2024 and 2025, only two clubs — PUC and AC Stains — could muster a full women's team and genuinely fulfil fixtures.
Tara Britton, a former Lisses and France player who subsequently joined PUC, said the only genuine match her new team played was against Stains.
The other teams either did not turn up, did so without enough players, or wanted to play with a tennis ball rather than a cricket ball.
The France Cricket website lists the results from 2024 and 2025 with PUC as the champions and Stains as the beaten "finalists."
But Britton said those seasons essentially amounted to a single match.
And then there is the question of the ICC development funding.
Numerous clubs told AFP that they never received any help from France Cricket.
Sankaran said the organisation even refused to contribute to the purchase of a plastic wicket or cricket nets, offering only a loan instead. — REUTERS

046d561938f16ab2: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 – Think about the first thing you do when you wake up. Do you check your messages, scroll through social media or catch up on the latest news?
For many Malaysians, going online has become second nature. We shop, bank, work, study and stay connected with family and friends, often without considering the risks involved.
But as the internet becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, one question matters more than ever: Are we doing enough to protect ourselves online?
From suspicious messages promising easy money to fake shopping websites, cyberbullying and personal data misuse, online threats can affect anyone, regardless of age or digital experience.
Why internet safety is becoming everyone’s concern
Being internet-savvy does not necessarily mean knowing how to stay safe online.

A scam message might appear to come from a familiar company. A fraudulent website could look almost identical to a legitimate online store. Even personal information shared innocently on social media could expose users to privacy and security risks.
For younger users, cyberbullying, harmful content and online grooming present additional dangers, particularly for children and teenagers still learning to navigate digital spaces.
Adults and senior citizens are not immune either, with financial scams and impersonation among the threats they may encounter.
Internet safety is no longer simply about protecting devices from viruses. It is also about safeguarding our identity, finances, privacy and wellbeing.
What is Kempen Internet Selamat?
Recognising the need for greater public awareness, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) introduced Kempen Internet Selamat (KIS) in January 2025.
The nationwide initiative aims to equip Malaysians with the knowledge and practical skills to use the internet safely, responsibly and ethically.
Its focus includes online scams, cyberbullying, misinformation, personal data protection and online sexual exploitation.
Rather than simply warning users about digital dangers, KIS encourages Malaysians to recognise potential threats and develop better online habits.
The campaign has also expanded its nationwide reach.
According to the latest MCMC figures as of October 2026, KIS had conducted 17,014 programmes nationwide, reaching more than 3.13 million participants since its introduction in 2025.
In 2026 alone, the campaign recorded 7,373 programmes, surpassing its annual target of 4,000 programmes, with 2,257,834 participants reached as of October 31.
Through educational activities, community engagement and practical demonstrations, the initiative seeks to make digital safety knowledge accessible to Malaysians of different ages and backgrounds.
A safer internet starts with everyday habits
Protecting yourself online does not always require advanced technical knowledge. Sometimes, small changes to everyday routines can make a difference.
Before clicking on a WhatsApp link, verify the sender and check whether the message is genuine.
When shopping online, check the seller’s credibility and avoid suspicious payment links.
Review social media privacy settings, use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication wherever possible.
Think twice before sharing personal information, including phone numbers, identification details or your current location.
For parents, online safety goes beyond limiting screen time. Regular conversations about children’s online experiences can help them recognise uncomfortable situations and seek help when needed.
Reporting suspicious online activities through appropriate channels can also help protect other users.
Building a safer digital Malaysia starts with awareness
The internet offers Malaysians countless opportunities, from digital businesses and education to easier access to financial services and information.
But enjoying these benefits also means understanding the risks and responsibilities that come with being connected.
Through its outreach to schools and communities, Kempen Internet Selamat plays an important role in promoting digital awareness and encouraging Malaysians to make informed decisions online.
However, creating a safer digital environment is a shared responsibility. Technology platforms, families, educators and individuals all have roles to play in protecting internet users.
Ultimately, KIS goes beyond teaching Malaysians how to avoid online threats. It aims to build a culture of digital awareness where safer, more responsible internet use becomes part of everyday life.
Because a safer internet depends not only on technology and regulations, but also on informed users who recognise risks, look out for one another and make better choices online.
5faeb595c9a2dcc6: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has attracted RM350.4 billion in approved investments across the services, manufacturing and primary sectors in the first nine months of 2026, up 20.7 per cent from RM290.3 billion a year earlier.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the 4,387 approved projects are expected to generate 152,090 jobs upon full implementation.
Foreign investments accounted for RM212.3 billion, or 60.6 per cent of total approvals, while domestic investments stood at RM138.1 billion.
The United States was the largest foreign investment source, contributing RM60 billion, more than five times the RM11.3 billion recorded in the corresponding period last year.
China followed with RM38.6 billion, Singapore RM38.5 billion, Japan RM24.4 billion and Australia RM12.6 billion.
Collectively, the five countries contributed RM174.1 billion, or 82 per cent of total foreign investment approvals.
The nine-month investment total represents 81.3 per cent of the revised RM431.1 billion approved for the whole of 2025.
Mida chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the performance demonstrated Malaysia's continued appeal despite global economic uncertainty.
He said the focus was on ensuring investments translated into high-value employment, stronger industrial capabilities and opportunities for local talent.
"These industries deepen our industrial capabilities, strengthen Malaysia's position in global value chains and create well-paying career opportunities for our people.

"Mida is also working closely with industry and education partners to ensure talent development keeps pace with investor needs. Investing in skills and higher-quality jobs is key to a stronger industrial ecosystem," he said in a statement today.
SERVICES LEAD INVESTMENT INFLOWS
The services sector attracted the largest share of investments at RM219.1 billion, accounting for 62.5 per cent of total approvals.
This represented a 14.2 per cent increase from RM191.7 billion in the same period last year, with 2,993 projects expected to generate 59,273 jobs.
Information and communications led the sector with RM133.5 billion, followed by real estate at RM47.9 billion and support services at RM19.3 billion.
Data centre and cloud computing projects accounted for RM123.5 billion across 86 projects, up 44.5 per cent year-on-year.
The projects represented 35.2 per cent of total approved investments, compared with 29.4 per cent in the corresponding period last year.
MANUFACTURING REBOUNDS
The manufacturing sector secured RM106.3 billion across 1,353 projects, marking a 13.3 per cent increase in investment value and a 53.1 per cent rise in project numbers.

The performance marked a turnaround from the 25.1 per cent decline in investment value recorded in the first half of 2026, supported by third-quarter approvals involving optical transceivers for AI data centres and liquefied natural gas processing.
The electrical and electronics (E&E) industry led manufacturing investments with RM40.8 billion, up 85.3 per cent year-on-year.

Other major contributors included petroleum products and petrochemicals at RM13.2 billion, machinery and equipment (RM9.4 billion), basic metal products (RM6.7 billion) and food manufacturing (RM6.4 billion).
Manufacturing projects are expected to generate 92,489 jobs, of which 72,111, or 78 per cent, will go to Malaysians.
Of the 34,529 managerial, technical, supervisory and skilled positions, 92.4 per cent are allocated to Malaysians.
Some 16,607 positions are expected to offer monthly salaries of at least RM5,000.
PRIMARY SECTOR SURGES
The primary sector recorded RM25 billion in approved investments, surging 420 per cent from RM4.8 billion a year earlier.
The amount also exceeded the sector's full-year 2025 investment total of RM14.2 billion by 76.9 per cent.
Domestic investments contributed RM13.9 billion, while foreign investments stood at RM11.1 billion.
Mining accounted for RM24.8 billion, mainly involving oil and gas exploration and development, while agriculture contributed about RM300 million.
JOHOR TOPS INVESTMENT DESTINATIONS

Johor emerged as the largest investment destination with RM99.7 billion in approvals, followed by Selangor at RM87.9 billion, Penang (RM41.1 billion), Kuala Lumpur (RM37.3 billion) and Sabah (RM19.5 billion).
Together, the five states accounted for 81.5 per cent of total approved investments.
Johor's approvals were driven by RM68.3 billion in services, mainly information and communications, and RM31.2 billion in manufacturing, led by E&E.
Selangor recorded the highest number of projects at 1,302, which are expected to create 34,971 jobs.

Mida said 87.4 per cent of the 6,202 manufacturing projects approved between 2021 and September 2026 had reached various stages of implementation, including production, factory construction or machinery installation.
As of October, Mida had 223 proposed projects worth RM41.2 billion under its purview, comprising 119 manufacturing projects valued at RM18.6 billion and 104 services projects worth RM22.6 billion.
It was also discussing potential investments worth RM60.5 billion.

437bc37c6de9c962: MANILA: The Philippines takes centre stage as Asean leaders and key global figures gather for crucial talks on the final day of the 49th Asean Summit.
United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in Manila at 5.30pm local time, making him the last world leader scheduled to arrive for the summit.
His arrival is scheduled half an hour after the closing ceremony begins at 5pm. The ceremony is expected to end at 5.45pm.
Trump is also expected to deliver remarks at a dinner with Asean leaders scheduled for 8.25pm.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived on Sunday to attend the Asean-China Summit, while Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined the Asean-India Summit the following day.
Several key meetings with dialogue partners are scheduled for the final day.
They include the 29th Asean Plus Three (APT) Summit, which began at 8.30am, followed by the fourth Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders' Meeting at 10.15am.
The 29th Asean-Japan Summit is scheduled for 11.15am, followed by the 13th Mekong-Japan Summit at 12.30pm and the 23rd Asean-India Summit at 1.15pm.
The programme continues with the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) at 2.30pm, bringing together regional leaders and dialogue partners to discuss issues of mutual interest.
The day's proceedings will include the closing ceremony of the 49th Asean Summit, during which the Philippines will formally hand over the Asean chairmanship to Singapore for 2027.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, as Asean chairman, is scheduled to deliver remarks at the ceremony.
The Asean-United States Special Summit will follow the closing ceremony, bringing the day's meetings to a close.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who returned to Malaysia yesterday to receive French President Emmanuel Macron, is scheduled to arrive back in Manila at 4.25pm today to attend the special summit and a dinner hosted by Marcos.
1cd4c72b818afc84: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction sector continues to expand in the third quarter of 2026, supported by strong private-sector activity, growing data centre developments and sustained demand for non-residential buildings.

Construction work done rose 9.0 per cent year-on-year to RM49.5 billion in the quarter, marking the 15th consecutive quarter of expansion, MBSB Research said, based on the Department of Statistics data.
The value of work done also increased 3.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter, bringing the total for the first nine months of 2026 to RM143.9 billion, up 8.8 per cent from a year earlier.
Non-residential buildings recorded the strongest growth, rising 21.1 per cent to RM15.7 billion, while special trades increased 13.2 per cent to RM6.2 billion.
The private sector remained the main growth driver, with construction work done rising 12.7 per cent to RM33.3 billion, compared with a 2.2 per cent expansion in public-sector activity.
Selangor and Johor accounted for 43.2 per cent of nationwide construction work done, reflecting the concentration of data centre and advanced industrial developments in both states.

MBSB Research said the latest figures indicated that data centre contract awards were translating into physical construction activity, although public infrastructure projects had yet to provide a comparable boost.

On the infrastructure front, the RM2.69 billion contract for the second civil and major infrastructure works package (CMC2) of the Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line brought the value of the project's three main packages to RM13.65 billion.

The package, awarded to the China Communications Construction Co-TRC-Ufuk consortium, covers a 5.5km connection from Macallum to Penang Sentral, including a 3.05km sea-crossing bridge linking Penang island to the mainland's rail and bus network.
This follows the RM7.93 billion CMC1 package secured by Gamuda Bhd-led SRS consortium, while the RM3.03 billion systems package was awarded to the MRCB-Theta Edge consortium.

With overall construction progress at about 16 per cent, MBSB Research expects Gamuda's billings to increase as civil works gather pace, while MRCB's contribution should accelerate following the initial design and mobilisation stages.

Looking ahead, MBSB Research said the next major public-sector opportunities include RM9 billion to RM12 billion worth of water infrastructure projects, comprising Northern Perak Water, Langat 2 Phase 2 and Sungai Rasau Phase 2.
Johor's proposed RM7 billion to RM8 billion elevated autonomous rapid transit system also represents a medium-term opportunity, pending greater clarity on funding and procurement.

On construction material costs, the firm said steel prices remained manageable, with average steel bar prices rising 4.1 per cent month-on-month to RM2,210 per tonne in October, although they remained 6.4 per cent below the May peak.

Bulk cement prices fell 1.2 per cent month-on-month to RM397 per tonne, while coal procurement costs stood at between US$80 and US$90 per tonne, posing a margin challenge amid softer average selling prices.

MBSB Research estimated that every sustained US$10 per tonne movement in coal costs could change Malayan Cement Bhd's annual earnings by about five to six per cent and its earnings before interest and tax margin by 130 basis points, assuming limited cost pass-through.
Despite cost pressures and uncertainty surrounding tighter US chip controls, the research house maintained a positive outlook on the construction sector.
It cited record data centre contract awards of RM18.24 billion in 2026, nearly double the previous year's level, alongside continued growth in construction activity.

The RM430 billion development expenditure allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan also provides a broader medium-term opportunity, spanning transport, water, power grid and East Malaysian infrastructure projects.
MBSB Research named Gamuda, Sunway Contruction Group Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd as its top picks, with buy recommendations and target prices of RM5.60, RM9.28 and RM3.32 respectively.

f81928cfe353f8b8: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction players with heavy exposure to data centre projects could face greater uncertainty following tighter United States (US) restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, although existing projects are unlikely to be derailed immediately.

MBSB Research said the new US Commerce Department rules, which seek to prevent restricted users from remotely accessing advanced American chips through overseas data centres, could raise compliance requirements and slow the rollout of future projects in Malaysia.

It said the immediate impact will likely be on graphics processing unit (GPU) deployment and capacity activation, with construction demand affected only if delays weakened tenant commitments or postponed subsequent development phases.
Projects backed by established US hyperscalers are expected to be better positioned to meet the new requirements.
Facilities relying on Chinese AI customers or less transparent GPU-as-a-Service arrangements could face longer licensing and customer-verification processes.

MBSB Research said exposure to data centre projects varied among major construction companies, with Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) having the highest concentration, while Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd had more diversified order books.
SunCon's outstanding data centre works were estimated at RM10.5 billion to RM11 billion, equivalent to 78-82 per cent of its RM13.4 billion order book.
IJM's remaining data centre works were estimated at RM1.8 billion to RM2.2 billion, representing 12 to 15 per cent of its RM14.5 billion order book.
Kerjaya Prospek's maiden data centre contract worth RM858 million accounted for 12 to 14 per cent of its RM6 billion backlog.

Gamuda had estimated data centre exposure of RM6.5 billion to RM7 billion, or a smaller 9.8 to 10.6 per cent of its RM66 billion order book, providing greater diversification through its infrastructure portfolio.
Despite the regulatory uncertainty, commitments from major US hyperscalers continue to underpin Malaysia's data centre investment pipeline.

Google plans to invest US$15 billion in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028, including additional campuses in Selangor and Negri Sembilan, alongside more than 1GW of clean-energy capacity and related water infrastructure.

Microsoft has committed US$2.2 billion over four years and is developing its SEA3 facility in Johor as its second Malaysian cloud region, while Amazon Web Services plans to invest US$6.2 billion through 2038.

However, MBSB Research cautioned that tighter chip controls and greater scrutiny of returns from AI investments could prompt hyperscalers to phase their capital expenditure more cautiously, particularly for expansion phases that have yet to be committed.

The firm said existing awarded projects and visible US-backed opportunities over the next 12 months should remain largely intact, although tighter controls could delay subsequent development phases and slow new contract awards.
It maintained a positive outlook on the construction sector, with Gamuda, SunCon and IJM as its top picks, carrying buy recommendations and target prices of RM5.60, RM9.28 and RM3.32 respectively.
97e183cf29c08ab1: KUALA LUMPUR: Former chief justice Zaki Azmi has warned that corruption can undermine investor confidence in Malaysia and destroy long-term business value, reflecting the importance of integrity and good governance to economic growth.

"Corruption is a corrosive crime which is condemned by civil law and prohibited by religion. More importantly, for businesses, it is a false economy that distorts competition and destroys long-term value.
"Maintaining integrity is easy when times are good. The true test comes when we are cornered," he said at the 2026 International CEO and Business Leaders Forum here today.
Zaki said there should be no compromise in upholding the law, even when a loved one is involved, as such situations present the true test of a person’s integrity.
He cited the example of Prophet Muhammad, who declared that even his own daughter, Fatimah, would not be exempt from the law if she committed theft.
Zaki said the Prophet was prepared to impose the prescribed punishment on his own daughter, underscoring the principle that nobody should be above the law.

The former top judge also warned that smaller economies face greater economic consequences when governance fails, with global markets sometimes penalising developing nations for lapses overlooked in larger economies.
He expressed concern that younger generations might normalise corruption, recalling his advice to university graduates against accepting even the smallest bribes.
"Don't ever be tempted to take even one sen for corruption," he recalled telling them, warning that accepting small payments could lead to increasingly serious misconduct.
He added that it was the responsibility of leaders to set an example, as "a fish rots from the head down".
Political uncertainty and investor confidence

Beyond corruption, Zaki said recent political developments following state elections in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Johor could also affect foreign investor confidence despite Malaysia's strong economic performance.
He said investors would question whether the same government would remain in office over the next five or 10 years, allowing sufficient time for them to realise returns on their investments.
"Investors do not necessarily care which political coalition governs a nation.
"What they require is policy continuity, the rule of law and the confidence that regulations will not shift overnight before they can realise a return on their capital."
He drew contrast with the UK, saying the latter remained an attractive investment destination despite several changes of prime minister in recent years.
He argued that larger economies could withstand political turbulence more easily, while smaller nations were more vulnerable to changes in investor sentiment.
In the Nov 14 Melaka election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured three and Pakatan Harapan (PH) four.
The result followed the BN-PN alliance's victory in Negeri Sembilan on Aug 1, where BN won 18 seats and PN took seven to secure a combined 25 seats in the 36-member assembly, leaving PH with 11.
In Johor's July 11 election, BN retained power with 48 of the 56 seats, while PH won eight and PN failed to secure any.

ff28df199bbed62a: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Oodles of noodles, bowlfuls of yong tau foo. Now that’s a table I would return to, time and again.
Such a table can be found at Yi Sou Mian Fen Gao, located in Seremban’s Oakland neighbourhood. As its name suggests, the shop specialises in mian fen gao (or min fan gou in Cantonese).

Don’t be confused while searching for the shop. While the English words on the signage states “Yi Sou Ban Mi” but its name in Chinese (二嫂麵粉糕) still translates to “Yi Sou Mian Fen Gao”; yi sou meaning “second sister-in-law” in Cantonese.
That particular dialect can be heard in full force when entering the shop full of customers. Not just the clientele but the courteous and friendly owner too.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Yi Sou Mian Fen Gao is located in Seremban’s Oakland neighbourhood. — Picture by CK Lim
Which is why you hear regulars ordering min fan gou and other dishes in Cantonese. It’s heartwarming for those from nearby Klang Valley or Cantonese folks like myself.
I love the poster that announces discreetly: “We Welcome Table Sharing”. It’s just a very neat way of saying they encourage the Hong Kong practice of daap toi or sharing a table with other patrons.
The boss takes pains to explain this when empty tables are scarce (turnover seems fast, however, so don’t fret if the shop looks full); this way hungry customers don’t have to wait long for a seat.

Once seated, we ordered our noodles first as the min fan gou are torn by hand and not made ahead of time. You could have thick or thin pan mee, yee mee, meehoon, hor fun… but honestly most regulars go for the min fan gou.

We ordered a bowl of this and another of bamboo noodles. Both dry málà as their Sichuan style spicy numbing sauce is supposed to tickle even the most fastidious of taste buds and revive dull appetites.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Shop full of customers. — Picture by CK Lim
(Spoiler: This turned out to be a fantastic decision though our lips are still smarting from the Sichuan peppercorns and chillies.)

The irregular pieces of min fan gou are perfectly chewy; the bamboo noodles — Cantonese egg noodles made from waterless dough, traditionally kneaded with a long bamboo pole — have that inimitable spring, that much sought after “QQ” texture.
For greens, there’s a choice of sayur manis or Chinese spinach; we always go with the former (also known as mani cai in Chinese) when it comes to pan mee.
Pair your bowl of noodles and bowls of naturally sweet ikan bilis rich broth with their housemade yong tau foo.
Every piece is stuffed with fish paste made from fresh ikan tenggiri (Spanish mackerel or ma gaau yu in Cantonese). Without mixing in denser minced pork, the filling is bouncier.
Yi Sou offers a variety of yong tau foo, from eggplant and bitter gourd to chilli and tofu. The usual suspects, naturally.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Bamboo noodles (left). Lotus and egg 'yong tau foo' (right). — Pictures by CK Lim

For something different, try their lotus and egg yong tau foo. The latter reminds me of the century egg yong tau foo at Kopitiam Tanka in Melaka, albeit Yi Sou’s version is a “safer” option for those who aren’t fans of the pei dan’s pungent aroma.
(Perilous or peerless, one’s reaction to century eggs might be the ultimate foodie personality test, no?)

Past their signature offerings, Yi Sou also does a fantastic job with their coffee and tea. I would go as far as saying their beverage menu marries both local kopi and teh with their not-so-distant Hong Kong cousins.

Certainly there’s a bit of the Hong Kong style coffee service here. Our server brings an empty cup and saucer to our table and pours coffee directly from a pitcher; the result is decidedly creamier with a lovely head foam.

The boss had recommended their signature kopi with Black & White evaporated milk, noting that this specific brand is popular in Hong Kong. Certainly the taste recalls that of a traditional cha chaan teng in Mong Kok.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Signature 'kopi' with Black & White evaporated milk (left). Black & White Gao Gao Cham (right). — Pictures by CK Lim
In lieu of my usual cham, I opted for Yi Sou’s Black & White Gao Gao Cham. Another drink that looks straight out of a cha chaan teng menu, this tastes like elevated iced yin-yong. Nice.
But the real stunner of our meal is something far more modest. Too often we simply order roti butter kaya and make do with ho-hum, limp renditions.
Here the bread comes either as toast or steamed; we go with the roti bakar, which arrives still crispy but not charred, unlike at some kopitiams. Cut into six squares, for bite-sized snacking.

The butter, they proudly remind us, is real butter and not a blended spread. (Which seems self-evident except nowadays so many kopitiams use the latter or margarine, that using the real deal has become a key differentiator.)
Best of all is their homemade kaya: green and grainy, made from real pandan leaves. Not too sweet, with a tinge of floral fragrance. Now that is the real deal.

Suffice to say, Yi Sou Mian Fen Gao hits the spot, from the food and drinks to the convivial Cantonese-speaking community. Come for the noodles and yong tau foo, but make sure to return for the butter and kaya toast.

a6e7dbd7c8067da3: SYDNEY: Australia said on Tuesday it will require tourists on working holiday visas to complete extra work in rural areas, as the government attempts to balance a reduction in migration with a shortage of labour in its farming and hospitality sectors.

Australia's Working Holiday Maker program — a popular rite of passage for young people from more than a dozen countries — will now require applicants to complete four months of rural work to remain in the country for a second year, up from the current three months.
"Working holiday makers make an important contribution to our economy, especially in agriculture, tourism and hospitality and in regional Australia," Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said.
"But when demand grows too fast, the government needs the tools to manage the program properly."
Rural employers in Australia are heavily reliant on backpackers to fill seasonal roles.
Under the program for 18-to-35-year-olds, Australia grants a one-year working holiday visa, extendable for a second and third year if the backpackers undertake regional work.
Backpackers typically work as nannies, waiters and in farming, among other retail and hospitality jobs.

Under a 2021 carve-out agreed by previous governments in both countries, the rural work rules do not apply to UK backpackers, which has led to a surge of British arrivals in Australia and a shortage of workers in regional areas.

Australia has already announced curbs on foreign students bringing partners and children to accompany them while they study and a ballot system for backpackers, amid growing debate in the country over high migration levels.
d847a259a83d7e6d: KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron, who is on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning.

4ae4fe6715f890f6: PETALING JAYA: Federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh today slammed Umno and PAS leaders who questioned the nominal RM1,000 land premium for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall's (KLSCAH) 99-year lease renewal.
Yeoh said certain Umno and PAS leaders were trying to racialise the matter by accusing her of "looking after her own race" by helping KLSCAH "escape" paying a higher land premium.

"This heritage building recorded an annual operational deficit of around RM400,000 due to the rise in maintenance costs, the building's aged structure and the growing need to upgrade safety and technical facilities.

Yeoh said KLSCAH still had to pay quit rent to the land office, assessment tax to Kuala Lumpur City Hall and income tax to the Inland Revenue Board.
She also slammed those who questioned KLSCAH for converting the land status, criticising them for failing to understand the value of heritage buildings in the capital city.
"If they understood their value, they would have upgraded and taken better care of the Sultan Abdul Samad building and Carcosa Seri Negara long ago.
"Who did that, in the end? Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. And they dared to question why we spent RM600 million for this purpose."

Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh had questioned the basis for the reduced premium for KLSCAH, saying the land was still worth RM4.67 million.
PAS's Kuala Terengganu MP Ahmad Amzad Hasim meanwhile urged the government to disclose the details of the reduced premium, including the conditions imposed and protection clauses.
Separately, academic Teo Kok Seong labelled the reduced premium as "unreasonable" and possibly controversial, saying the original estimate of RM4.67 million would have been based on concrete grounds.
27569fbeca9c6aea: TAIPEI: The timing of Washington's US$14 billion arms sales package to Taiwan is "very much up to" President Donald Trump and will not be affected by the US midterm results, according to a Taiwanese government official.
Taiwan has been waiting months for Trump to approve the record sale of weapons and equipment that the island says it needs to strengthen its defence capabilities to deter a potential Chinese attack.
Beijing claims the island democracy is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
Trump has stalled the arms sale, saying in May it could be used as a bargaining chip with China, as the two superpowers tried to ease trade tensions.
"When it comes to time, I think it's very much up to... President Trump," said Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi.
Taiwan enjoys "very strong bipartisan support" from Congress, and this month's midterm results, which saw Democrats win control of the House and Senate, would not affect the timing, Chen said.
The Trump administration had to consider "many factors" when it came to arms sales to Taiwan, including the Middle East war.
"We respect that, but at the same time, we express that we really have an urgent need for those capabilities," Chen said.
Patriot missiles, an automated command and control system and a 360-degree air defence radar system are among the items in the US$14 billion package.
Chen said Taiwan had "very good direct communication" with the Trump administration and "we are reassured that that will not change".
"This could be just a matter of time before" the sale is approved, either as one package or in smaller parcels, he said.
Taiwan 'structurally important'
Trump is expected to meet Chinese president Xi Jinping for the third and fourth time this year at an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen this week and at the G20 in the United States in December.
While Taiwan has been on the agenda at previous talks between the rival leaders, Chen brushed off concerns about the upcoming meetings.
"We are very confident and very comfortable with our relationship with the US and with other like-minded partners," Chen said.
"We are structurally important, and our people (are) committed to our own defence. I think this (is) what matters the most," he said.
"And Taiwan stands in the middle of the whole AI revolution. I think that now almost every leader in the world understands the situation."
Taiwan is a powerhouse in the global semiconductor industry, producing nearly all of the most advanced chips for companies including Nvidia and Apple.

After Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who US intelligence agencies believe is spying for Beijing, Chen said the case underlines the need to be "very vigilant about China".
China is "very aggressive" when it comes to stealing intellectual property and technology to get around export controls, Chen said.
Huang, who regularly visited Taiwan to see Nvidia's clients, including TSMC, and had been seen in the capital Taipei with the Chinese woman, would be welcome back to the island, said Chen.
"He certainly will be welcome but I think... every business leader in the world has to learn this lesson that China is trying to poach your trade secrets," he said.
"They are going to arrange (a) spy in your life so that they can get easier access."
Beijing has rejected the allegations as "entirely baseless".
China is in a race for tech dominance against the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Taiwan has long accused China of carrying out espionage activities on the island, including targeting its tech sector.

26332e7b795c854b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysian households are expected to face growing price pressures in 2027 as inflation remains elevated and economic growth moderates, according to a new consumer outlook by Fitch Solutions unit, BMI.

BMI said consumers are likely to encounter a more challenging spending environment next year after revising its inflation forecast for Malaysia to 2.0 per cent from 1.8 per cent previously. Elevated prices are expected to continue weighing on household purchasing power and restrain discretionary spending.

The report noted that inflation remains above pre-pandemic levels and that the pressure on households would be compounded by high household debt and related debt-servicing costs. It also forecast limited monetary policy relief, with Bank Negara Malaysia expected to maintain its policy rate at 2.75 per cent until the first quarter of 2027.

At the same time, BMI expects Malaysia's economic growth to ease in the third quarter of 2026. The research house forecast real GDP growth to slow to 5.2 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter from 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter, citing mixed high-frequency economic indicators.

According to the report, export growth strengthened from 45.5 per cent year-on-year in June to 54.5 per cent in September, while retail sales growth moderated from 4.2 per cent in June to 3.8 per cent in August.

BMI also said headline inflation edged lower from 1.9 per cent year-on-year in August to 1.8 per cent in September, but is expected to move closer to 2.0 per cent in October due to rising housing and food costs.

Despite the expected pressures, the report projected household spending to remain resilient. Real household spending growth is forecast to ease only marginally to 4.07 per cent in 2027 from 4.08 per cent in 2026.
BMI said it would also be monitoring the release of Malaysia's third-quarter GDP data and inflation figures as indicators of the country's consumer outlook going into 2027.

81209be5e94fd288: SINGAPORE, Nov 17 — Singapore said Tuesday it was seeking “trusted access” to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres.

The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.
“We are studying the details of this new measure carefully,” Singapore’s ministries overseeing digital development and energy, trade and industry said in a joint statement.
“We are engaging affected companies to understand the potential impact on their businesses,” the ministries added.

The city-state was also talking to the “relevant US authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure, as well as exploring how to facilitate trusted access for Singapore companies”, the ministries added.
One loophole allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

Under the new rule, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.
The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US commerce department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there.

The scandal erupted on November 8 when The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang – who are not related – were romantically linked, and that some within the US government suspected she might be a spy for China.
The city-state is battling to contain the damage to its reputation as a stable rules-based business hub and trusted destination for multinational investment.

“We take our international reputation seriously and do not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities, including export controls,” Singapore said.

The government added it would continue to “safeguard continued access to advanced semiconductors and computing capabilities for legitimate companies operating here, and act against those who flout our laws.”
Megaspeed on Sunday said Alice Huang left the firm more than a year ago. — AFP
eb81dfbdb71f7677: KUALA LUMPUR: Presiden Perancis Emmanuel Macron yang dalam rangka lawatan rasmi dua hari ke Malaysia bermula semalam diberi sambutan negara di Dataran Merdeka hari ini.
Ketibaan Macron bersama isterinya, Brigitte Macron pada 9.30 pagi disambut Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dan isteri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Turut hadir kedua-dua Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi dan Fadillah Yusof.
Istiadat sambutan dimulakan dengan nyanyian lagu kebangsaan Perancis dan Malaysia oleh Pancaragam Pusat Rejimen Askar Melayu Diraja (RAMD) diketuai Muhamad Fauzee Japar.
Macron kemudian memeriksa kawalan kehormat yang terdiri daripada tiga pegawai dan 103 anggota lain-lain pangkat daripada Batalion Pertama RAMD diketuai Adibadiuezshah Ahmad.

Menariknya, sambutan negara kali ini berlangsung di lokasi bersejarah Dataran Merdeka, yang sinonim dengan perjuangan kemerdekaan negara dan menjadi antara mercu tanda utama ibu negara, berbeza daripada beberapa istiadat sambutan rasmi pemimpin asing sebelum ini yang diadakan di Putrajaya atau Istana Negara.
Lawatan itu merupakan kunjungan rasmi pertama Macron ke Malaysia sejak memegang jawatan sebagai presiden Perancis pada Mei 2017.
Kunjungan itu dijangka membuka lembaran baharu dalam hubungan Malaysia-Perancis apabila kedua-dua negara berhasrat meningkatkan hubungan sedia terjalin kepada perkongsian strategik.

Antara bidang kerjasama diberi tumpuan ialah pertahanan dan keselamatan, mineral kritikal, peralihan tenaga, aeronautik dan angkasa lepas, kecerdasan buatan (AI), keselamatan siber serta semikonduktor.
Lawatan itu juga menyusuli momentum lawatan rasmi Anwar ke Perancis pada Julai 2025, iaitu yang pertama oleh ketua kerajaan Malaysia ke negara itu dalam tempoh 15 tahun.

Perancis merupakan rakan dagang ke-10 terbesar Malaysia dan ketiga terbesar dalam kalangan negara Kesatuan Eropah (EU), dengan jumlah perdagangan dua hala mencecah €4.7 bilion (kira-kira RM21.23 bilion) pada 2025, meningkat 11% berbanding 2024.

155d4ab99c3bab82: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysians lost RM6.95 billion to online scams between 2023 and August 2026, according to the latest figures disclosed by the Home Ministry in Parliament.

In a written parliamentary reply dated November 1, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police recorded 181,750 online fraud cases over the nearly four-year period, with both case numbers and losses surging in 2025.

“In terms of losses, the total amount recorded for the period from 2023 to August 2026 stood at RM6.95 billion. Losses in 2023 totalled RM1.22 billion, rising to RM1.57 billion in 2024 and RM2.97 billion in 2025,” he said.
Between January and August 2026, victims lost RM1.18 billion, the reply added.
Case numbers rose slightly from 34,495 in 2023 to 35,368 in 2024, before nearly doubling to 66,204 in 2025.
From January to August 2026, police logged another 45,683 cases, Saifuddin said.
By category, telecommunications scams recorded the most cases at 69,195, followed by e-commerce fraud at 47,221. Love scams accounted for the fewest, at 3,540 cases.

The ministry said it viewed the escalation of online fraud seriously, noting that commercial cybercrime remains one of the country’s main law enforcement challenges because of the scale of losses suffered by victims.

600f4eaafa066a6b: LONDON, Nov 17 — As UK leader Andy Burnham prepares for a crunch EU summit this week, familiar faces from Britain’s Brexit wars are back, seeking to scupper his determination to forge closer ties to the bloc.
The Labour prime minister hopes to ink a reset with European chiefs in Brussels on Friday, cementing his pledge to secure a better relationship a decade after Britain voted to leave.

Ahead of the meeting, pro-Brexit voices from the 2016 vote are reorganising, concerned by Burnham’s reset plans and flirting with the idea that Britain could one day seek to rejoin the European Union.

In a speech late Monday, the British leader – who replaced Keir Starmer in July – said Britain had left the bloc in 2020 on “bad terms” and needed “to consider whether the relationship we have now is right”.
“It’s like the emperor’s new clothes where no one is prepared to say the obvious truth,” he added, arguing “we have lost more than we have gained in the last 10 years”.
“The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain,” Burnham said, reiterating his criticism that it has made the country poorer and contributed to higher immigration.
He noted this Friday’s summit would focus on securing three agreements, to cut red tape for food exports, link the two sides’ emissions-trading schemes and finalise a “youth experience scheme”.

But breaking with several years of taboo on the issue, Burnham suggested going further longer-term, pledging that post-summit London will “initiate a discussion with our EU partners about options” for the future relationship.
He added the talks “will take time” and he will present “options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next parliament” after the next general election, due by 2029.
“At every stage the British people will be the boss,” Burnham added.
‘Madness’
Burnham’s stance has been increasingly spooking Brexit’s backers.
Ahead of the speech, former premier Boris Johnson – a key “leave” campaigner who later negotiated the terms of Britain’s exit – told the Telegraph it was “madness” to reopen the debate.
He insisted the country would back Brexit again in another referendum – despite polls suggesting the opposite.
His comments echoed those of one of his predecessors David Cameron, who as prime minister called the EU referendum, campaigned for Britain to stay, and then resigned when he lost.
Last week, Cameron urged Burnham not to trigger a “decade-long debate” about rejoining the EU that he said would be “very long and painful”.
Burnham has committed to his predecessor Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.
But the issue has the potential to split his ruling centre-left Labour.
One party MP told AFP it should just “go for it” and put a commitment to rejoining in its manifesto for the next election.
However, some lawmakers in Brexit-supporting areas want Burnham to shut down the debate altogether, highlighting divisions within the ruling party, never mind the country.
Last week, one of Johnson’s former Brexit advisers, Oliver Lewis, launched a new campaign called “Stay Out”.
He said the UK leader will on Friday “sign a deal that sends more money to Brussels, hands back control of our own laws and opens the door to more immigration”.
Meanwhile, the Telegraph reported that former pro-Brexit campaign group “Leave.EU” is planning to relaunch under the name “Enough Official”.
“The UK really needs a debate about the world in 2026 rather than rehashing the same arguments from the same people as 10 years ago,” David Henig, an expert on UK-EU relations, told AFP.
“Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and Trump’s attacks on world trade are obvious new factors that have happened since then. Meanwhile, the economic benefits promised have not materialised.” — AFP

a48110b0a8da9f82: SINGAPORE: Asian shares followed Wall Street lower on Tuesday, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips, escalating the race for technological dominance.
South Korea's tech-heavy KOSPI slid 2% shortly after the open, while Taiwan stocks fell 1.4%.
Japan's Nikkei eased 1% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan extended early losses to last trade down 1.2%.

Overnight, Washington said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia. The new rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to data centres like those in Thailand and Malaysia that Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models.

The move came just days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman who worked at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that rents computing power at its data centers. It has come under scrutiny for possible illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China.

"This is a meaningful escalation because it extends restrictions from physically buying advanced chips to accessing their computing power remotely," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

"The impact could be significant for providers heavily reliant on Chinese customers training advanced AI models. They could face lower utilisation, weaker pricing and delays to expansion, while licensing uncertainty could make financing new projects harder."
Markets in China and Hong Kong slid, with the CSI300 blue-chip index down 0.5%, while the Shanghai Composite Index lost 0.65%.
The Hang Seng Tech Index shed roughly 2%.

A key moment for markets on Tuesday will be Nvidia's earnings after the bell, with investors watching for signs of whether its debt-fuelled AI spending will continue into 2027 and how Huang's departure could affect the company's influence across the AI ecosystem.

"With a roughly 7.8% implied move and a strong beat-and-raise already embedded, the bar looks increasingly tied to forward growth, AI ecosystem financing and export-control risk rather than the quarter alone," said Torsten Sippel, UBS's head of voice cash trading for the Americas.
US stock futures edged higher in Asia, with Nasdaq futures up 0.35% and S&P 500 futures adding 0.13%.
EUROSTOXX 50 futures, DAX futures and FTSE futures slid roughly 0.6% each.

Concerns about the AI outlook continued to roil the metals market, with copper prices falling to their lowest levels in more than four months overnight. Shares of Australian-listed miner Capstone Copper Corp tumbled nearly 6% to an eight-month low.
Dollar gets Fed lift

The US dollar rose to its highest point since April 2025 on Tuesday, helped by growing bets on more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes as inflationary pressures in the world's largest economy persist.

Markets now see a Fed hike next month as a certainty, and are pricing in a slim chance of a 50-basis-point move, with recent hawkish remarks from policymakers reinforcing expectations of tighter monetary policy.

"After all, nothing in the economic data since last week would warrant such a turn following the hawkish calls by the senior Fed staffers offered last week."
The strength in the dollar left the yen struggling near the key 160 level, leaving traders on alert for any intervention from Japanese authorities to shore up the currency.
The euro bottomed out at US$1.0985, its lowest level since April 2025.

The Australian dollar last bought US$0.6737, little changed after minutes from the Reserve Bank of Australia's November board meeting released on Tuesday showed the majority of members judged that a hike this month was needed as inflation risks were still skewed to the upside and financial conditions might not be as restrictive as required.
In commodities, oil prices fell as expectations of a supply surplus - fuelled by recovering Middle East exports - overshadowed concerns about continued attacks on tankers in the region.
Brent crude futures slid 0.9% to US$91.62 a barrel, while US crude lost 0.8% to US$85.05 per barrel.

e6219f5de996df51: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace has clarified that Datuk Ismail Lasim remains Menteri Besar pending royal assent, stressing that any resignation only takes effect after it is accepted by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in accordance with the state constitution.

In a statement today, the palace said it had taken note of a statement issued by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir on Nov 16 regarding Ismail's purported resignation from the post.
The palace said the statement appeared to be based on a copy of a resignation letter that was in Zambry's possession.

The palace also revealed that Ismail had earlier been granted an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar after making a request to do so.
It said the Ruler's private secretary informed Ismail via WhatsApp at 8.38pm on Nov 16 that his request had been approved, and that he had acknowledged receipt of the message.
The audience has been scheduled for 10am on Nov 20.
According to the palace, the approval for the audience was conveyed about 80 minutes before Zambry's social media posting announcing the resignation.
The palace further said it had yet to verify the authenticity of the resignation letter, which Zambry had stated was signed by Ismail.
The clarification comes amid heightened political attention in Negeri Sembilan following the announcement that Ismail had stepped down as Menteri Besar.
f8e66cc5fb152ae3: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 — The USS Theodore Roosevelt is operating in the Middle East, the US military said on Monday, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups in the region to three.

The Roosevelt and the ships accompanying it add to the already large US naval presence in the region, which includes two other carriers – the George H.W. Bush and the George Washington – and more than a dozen destroyers.

“The aircraft carrier is currently operating in the CENTCOM area of responsibility as part of a scheduled deployment,” Central Command – which is responsible for US forces in the Middle East – said in a post on X.

The carrier’s deployment to the Middle East comes during a flareup in the more than eight-month-long Iran war, with Tehran saying Sunday that its forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a helicopter base in the Gulf kingdom of Bahrain.
Bahrain’s military said it intercepted the drones, “preventing them from reaching their intended targets.”

The Islamic republic also fired drones at Bahrain on Friday – the first strikes since September against countries in the energy-rich Gulf, which has been heavily targeted in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
CENTCOM said it shot down two Iranian drones that day, reporting no casualties or damage.
Efforts to end the Middle East war have made little headway.

Tehran has insisted that Washington meet conditions including the release of frozen assets abroad, sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has blockaded the waterway, which is a vital global energy conduit, since the start of the war, but has said it is ready to reopen it within two days if Washington agrees to its terms.
US President Donald Trump has said he plans to discuss the war at a trilateral meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin this week.

Trump’s Republican Party suffered major losses in midterm congressional elections that both the president and Vice President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war, which has sharply driven up prices and is widely unpopular in the United States.

Washington has appeared to dial back threats of renewed strikes in the wake of the midterms, but Trump said last week that a deal with Iran on ending the war was unnecessary, and that he had directed Vance to focus on anti-fraud efforts instead. — AFP
0464225e47a1e5ce: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has urged Indonesia to either compensate Malaysia for losses arising from this year’s haze crisis or agree to the formation of a permanent trans-boundary firefighting task force with the authority to enter Indonesian forests immediately to combat fires.

In a statement today, Lim said Malaysia should accept the apology offered by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to Malaysia and Singapore over the prolonged haze episode in the spirit of good neighbourly relations and ASEAN solidarity.
However, he said Indonesia could not disclaim responsibility for the duration and impact of the crisis, which he said had been worsened by this year’s Super El Nino conditions.
Lim claimed that Malaysia had suffered welfare losses of RM8 billion linked to health impacts and economic losses of RM5 billion as a result of the haze.

He cited a study commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers, which estimated that severe air pollution could reduce international tourist arrivals by up to eight per cent and jeopardise the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign, with potential losses of up to RM5 billion in tourism-related gross domestic product.

According to Lim, the estimated RM8 billion in welfare losses reflected the economic cost associated with premature mortality risks and was linked to an estimated 1,700 premature deaths among Malaysians.

He said measures such as the use of air purifiers were essential during severe haze episodes and reiterated his earlier proposal for a RM1,000 tax rebate for the purchase of air purifiers to help protect vulnerable groups, particularly young children and senior citizens.

Lim said that if Indonesia was unable to provide compensation, it should agree to the establishment of a Permanent Trans-Boundary Haze Relief Task Force comprising trained personnel capable of undertaking immediate firefighting operations in Indonesian forests.
He said such a mechanism was necessary to prevent haze from becoming a recurring annual disaster in the region.

The former finance minister also called on Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to formally convey the proposal to Indonesia, arguing that a standing regional firefighting force with rapid deployment powers would enable ASEAN to respond more effectively to forest fires and trans-boundary haze incidents.
He added that concerns over national sovereignty should not stand in the way of practical solutions to address a problem that continues to affect millions of people across the region.

8f60598a25ce8ee9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Online scam syndicates are increasingly exploiting financially vulnerable university and college students by recruiting them as mule account holders, sometimes offering payments of as little as RM40.

Kosmo reported Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO) secretary-general Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim saying the trend has become more prevalent in several states, particularly among students in the Klang Valley, Selangor and Penang.
He said syndicates specifically target students from low-income families who are struggling to meet their daily expenses, using various pretexts to gain access to their banking information.
Among the latest tactics is the use of digital bank accounts, which can be opened online with minimal verification requirements such as a selfie and a copy of an identity card.
The ease of registration has enabled scammers to adapt their methods, moving away from the traditional practice of renting or buying physical ATM cards.
“These are modern-day mule account tactics. The modus operandi has evolved significantly,” Hishamuddin said.
He said students are commonly approached through advertisements for part-time jobs, paid surveys or education loan schemes.

In one frequently reported scam, students are instructed to open a bank account as part of a supposed recruitment process. Once the account is created, they are informed that they were unsuccessful in securing the job, unaware that the account may later be used for illegal transactions.

Other victims are tricked into providing personal details under the guise of participating in surveys, only to discover later that the information had been used to facilitate banking activities without their knowledge.

Hishamuddin said students seeking financial aid were also vulnerable. Some are persuaded to disclose online banking usernames and passwords after being told the details are needed for loan disbursements.
“The victims are often in urgent need of money and do not question the requests,” he said.
Many only realise they have become linked to criminal activities when contacted by police investigators or when their bank accounts are frozen following fraud complaints.
Beyond the immediate financial consequences, victims may face multiple investigations and long-term repercussions, including potential criminal records.

The issue has surfaced in several court cases involving students. Among them was a law student who was fined after admitting to allowing his bank account to be used for unlawful transactions, while another college student was charged with acting as a mule account holder for an online scam syndicate.

The growing problem had earlier prompted Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to warn that increasing numbers of students were being recruited by scam networks, with some allegedly offered monthly payments of between RM1,000 and RM2,000 in return for the use of their bank accounts.
